records.content: Digestive Health Severe COVID-19 May Leave Lasting Digestive Problems Severe COVID-19 may raise the risk of gut problems for up to two years, including bleeding, ulcers, acid reflux and other digestive conditions. Digestive Health Health Center Written by Dr. Himanshi Porwal , BDS Medically Reviewed by Dr. Sunil Shroff , MBBS, MS, FRCS (UK), D. Urol (Lond) Edited by Colleen Fleiss , M.Sc | Fact-checked by Dr. Shanmathi Rajendran , BDS ✓ Medically Reviewed ✓ Fact Checked Last Updated on Nov 07, 2026 Your reading guide Tap Listen and the guide reads this article aloud. Use A+ and A− at the side to change the text size. About Many of us know the feeling of a gut that will not settle after a bad fever. A bit of acidity, loose motions, a stomach that refuses to take food. Most people blame the last meal and move on. But a large new study from England suggests that after severe COVID-19, the gut can stay under strain for much longer than we think. Did You Know? Severe COVID-19 can affect gut health for up to two years after hospitalization, with some digestive conditions, including gut bleeding, remaining more common even after recovery. #covid19 #guthealth #digestivehealth #longcovid #covidrecovery #gutsymptoms #ibs #vaccination #postcovidsymptoms #healthresearch #medindia Researchers studied about 18.4 million adults and tracked 10 digestive conditions, including bleeding in the upper and lower gut, pancreatitis , appendicitis, acid reflux, indigestion, ulcers, fatty liver disease , gallstones and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). People who had been hospitalized with COVID-19 had a clearly higher rate of these conditions, and the extra risk was still visible up to two years later. The numbers are worth a look. According to the study, upper gut bleeding was about 20 times more common in the first four weeks after hospitalized COVID-19 than in the comparison period. Even in weeks 53 to 102, it was still about 1.9 times higher. People who were vaccinated before they caught COVID-19 had a smaller rise in risk than people who were unvaccinated. How Big Is The Gut Risk After Severe COVID-19? According to the BMJ journal study by Al Arab and colleagues (2026), the risk is biggest soon after infection and shrinks over time, but it does not vanish for people who were hospitalized. The team used health records of 24 million people in England. They compared how often each digestive problem happened after COVID-19 with how often it happened before COVID-19 or in people who never had it.( 1 ✔ ✔ Trusted Source Al Arab M, Cezard G, Crooks C, Wei Y, Horne E, Palmer TM, et al. Impact of COVID-19 on gastrointestinal disease in vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals: a population-based cohort study in England. BMJ Public Health. 2026;4(4) Go to source ) They then split people into three groups: those infected before vaccines (18,422,781 people), vaccinated people (14,948,727) and unvaccinated people (3,479,043) during the Delta wave in 2021. The study used a measure called the adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) to compare the risk of bleeding between groups. A value of 1 means the risk is the same. A value of 2 means twice the risk, while 20 means 20 times the risk. Your gut after COVID-19 COVID-19 Can Affect Your Gut Too! The effects may not always end when the infection does. A large study in England found that people hospitalised with COVID-19 had a greater risk of several digestive problems. Some increased risks were still seen much later. Step 1 • Explore Which Parts of the Gut Can Be Affected? Tap the numbered spots to discover the digestive conditions examined in the study. Stomach and food pipe These areas help move and break down food. The study examined problems that can affect this part of digestion. Acid reflux Indigestion Ulcers Upper GI bleeding Tap any numbered spot on the illustration to explore another area. The highlighted areas are simplified illustrations. Some digestive conditions can involve more than one part of the digestive tract. Step 2 • Follow the timeline How Long Can the Risk Remain Higher? The study followed digestive health after COVID-19. Tap each time point to see what was reported. The first four weeks 20.1× Hospitalised people in the pre-vaccination group had 20.1 times the relative risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding compared with the study's reference group. This is a relative-risk comparison, not a 20.1-in-100 chance. It does not mean that most people who had COVID-19 developed bleeding. Step 3 • Compare the findings Did Hospitalisation Make a Difference? The biggest increases in upper gut bleeding risk were seen among people who needed hospital care. Before vaccines Relative risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the first four weeks after COVID-19 Hospitalised 20.1× Not hospitalised 1.92× All COVID-19 cases 3.77× The hospitalised group had the highest relative risk in this comparison. These are adjusted hazard ratios reported by the study. The bars are scaled to a maximum of 22 for visual comparison. A higher ratio does not tell us the absolute chance of developing bleeding. The key takeaways Your Gut Health Deserves Attention After COVID-19 Here are the main messages from the study. Severe illness mattered The largest increases were seen after hospitalisation. Effects may last Some increased risks were still seen beyond one year. Do not ignore symptoms Persistent or worrying digestive symptoms need medical advice. One important point: This was an observational study. It found links between COVID-19 and digestive conditions, but it cannot prove that COVID-19 directly caused every condition. A higher relative risk also does not mean that the condition is common. Based on a population-based cohort study published in BMJ Public Health (2026). What Stands Out? Hospitalisation matters most: A hospital stay meant a far bigger jump in risk than a milder illness. The risk fades but lingers: After hospitalized COVID-19, upper gut bleeding was still 1.90 times higher in weeks 53 to 102. After non-hospitalized COVID-19 it was 1.34 times higher. Lower gut bleeding followed the same pattern: In the first four weeks after hospitalisation, it was 13.7 times higher in the prevaccination group. Age changes the picture: For upper gut bleeding in weeks 1 to 4, the aHR was 1.69 in adults aged 18 to 39 and 5.04 in those aged 60 to 79. The absolute numbers are small: Excess risk of upper gut bleeding 28 weeks after COVID-19 was 159 per 100,000 people in the prevaccination group, 60 in the vaccinated group and 112 in the unvaccinated group. So a high ratio does not mean most people will get these problems. It means that, in a big population, a small number of extra cases appear, mostly in older and sicker people. The authors also note limits, hospitalized patients have more tests and scans, so more problems get recorded. The prevaccination group was infected earlier in the pandemic and is not directly comparable with the other two. But they say these issues alone are unlikely to explain the long-lasting rise after hospitalized COVID-19. Does Vaccination Really Protect The Gut? According to Hong and colleagues in Frontiers in Medicine , vaccination was linked to fewer gut symptoms during COVID-19 in people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), a long-term condition that includes Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. ( 2 ✔ ✔ Trusted Source Hong Y, Che T, Shen X, Chen J, Wang K, Zhao L, et al. The association of three vaccination doses with reduced gastrointestinal symptoms after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infections in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. Front Med. 2024;11:1377926 Go to source ) Researchers surveyed 536 people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from three hospitals in Shanghai who had COVID-19 during the 2022 Omicron wave. They checked whether new digestive problems were linked to the number of COVID-19 vaccine doses received. All participants had received inactivated vaccines. New gut symptoms were reported by 53.7% of unvaccinated patients, 54.8% of those who received one dose and 53% of those who received two doses. The rate was lower (37.8%) among those who received three doses. After considering other factors, three vaccine doses were linked to about 44% lower odds of developing gut symptoms compared with no vaccination. Diarrhoea , nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite were also less common. One or two doses did not show a clear benefit. The study shows a link, not proof that vaccination prevented these symptoms. The benefit also appeared weaker in people taking medicines that suppress the immune system . What does this mean? COVID-19 vaccination may reduce digestive problems in people with IBD, but it does not prevent them completely. Can the Vaccine Itself Cause Stomach Problems? A case report in Cureus described a 41-year-old man who developed diarrhoea and stomach pain one day after a Moderna booster. He was diagnosed with bowel inflammation and treated with antibiotics .( 3 ✔ ✔ Trusted Source Ajmera K, Bansal R, Wilkinson H, Goyal L. Gastrointestinal complications of COVID-19 vaccines. Cureus. 2022;14(4):e24070 Go to source ) The authors also reviewed US vaccine safety reports and found 26,822 reports of diarrhoea and 10,625 reports of stomach pain among more than 250 million vaccinated people. What Should be Understood? These reports do not prove that the vaccine caused the symptoms. Most reported problems were described as mild and short-lived. A single case cannot show how common serious stomach problems are. The authors concluded that vaccine benefits outweigh the risks, but people with existing gut problems may need closer monitoring Why Does Severe COVID-19 Cause Gut Bleeding? Bleeding is the most worrying gut problem linked to COVID-19, so it helps to know why it happens. According to the review in Gastroenterology Clinics of North America , gut bleeding occurs in about 1.5% to 3.0% of people hospitalized with COVID-19. It usually shows up after admission, not as the first sign of illness. ( 4 ✔ ✔ Trusted Source Cappell MS, Friedel DM. Gastrointestinal bleeding in COVID-19-infected patients. Gastroenterol Clin North Am. 2022;52(1):77-102 Go to source ) The review describes a few main causes: Irritated gut lining: The virus enters cells through ACE2 receptors, which are plentiful in the stomach and intestines. This can cause inflammation and small erosions, usually with mild bleeding. Stress ulcers: Very sick patients with severe pneumonia can develop ulcers or stress gastritis in the stomach. This is the main cause of serious upper gut bleeding. Poor blood flow to the bowel: COVID-19 makes blood more likely to clot, which can lead to ischaemic colitis, where part of the colon is starved of blood. This is a common cause of lower gut bleeding. Hospital medicines: Steroids and blood thinners, often needed in severe COVID-19, can raise the chance of bleeding. The reassuring part is that this bleeding is usually mild to moderate, often settles on its own, and rarely adds to the risk of death. This fits with the English study. The people with the highest gut risk were those who were already very sick enough to be in hospital, where all these factors come together. How Common Are Gut Symptoms After You Recover? Quite common, according to a community survey from Saudi Arabia. In the SAGE Open Medicine study, 409 adults in the Aseer region filled in an online questionnaire. About 64% had gut symptoms during their COVID-19 illness, and about half (49.6%) still had some gut symptoms after recovering. The most common were diarrhoea, nausea, loss of appetite and abdominal pain , each reported by roughly 11% to 13%. ( 5 ✔ ✔ Trusted Source Alzahrani MA, Altalhiyyah KS, Albariqi MM, Alkhayri MA, Alshahrani SA, Alnasser SS, et al. Prevalence of gastrointestinal symptoms after recovery from COVID-19: a questionnaire-based study in the Aseer region. SAGE Open Med. 2025;13:20503121251314067 Go to source ) Most of these symptoms were short. Among people who had symptoms after recovery, about 63% said they lasted less than a week. Still, some people had them for two to four weeks. The study also looked at who was more likely to have lingering symptoms. It uses “odds ratios”, where a number above 1 means higher odds: Gut symptoms during infection: about 10 times higher odds of gut symptoms afterward. Needing hospital care: about 6 times higher odds. Not working in healthcare: about 4 times higher odds than healthcare workers. Males: about 1.9 times higher odds. Age: 67.9% of people over 50 had symptoms after recovery, against 43.6% of those aged 18 to 30. Because this was an online self-reported survey, people may not remember their symptoms accurately, so the numbers are best seen as a rough guide. Still, the pattern matches the English study. More severe illness and older age mean more gut trouble later. Can COVID-19 Lead To IBS-Like Problems? Yes, in a small number of people. A study from India looked at exactly this. According to Golla and colleagues in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology , researchers at AIIMS, New Delhi followed 320 patients after COVID-19 and compared them with 320 healthy family members and 280 healthy health workers who had no COVID-19.( 6 ✔ ✔ Trusted Source Golla R, Vuyyuru S, Kante B, Kumar P, Thomas DM, Makharia G, et al. Long-term gastrointestinal sequelae following COVID-19: a prospective follow-up cohort study. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2022;21(3):789-796 Go to source ) The results over time: At 1 month: 36 patients (11.3%) had new symptoms of a functional gut disorder, meaning real symptoms such as pain, bloating or diarrhoea without visible damage. At 3 months: 27 patients (8.4%) still had them. At 6 months: 21 patients (6.6%) still had them. Among the healthy comparison groups: none developed these problems. At 3 months, the most common diagnoses were IBS (2.5%), functional diarrhoea (2.2%) and functional indigestion (1.9%). Moderate to severe COVID-19 and having gut symptoms during the illness were the main risk factors. In 8 of the 27 people with persistent symptoms, tests showed trouble absorbing a type of sugar called xylose , which suggests there may be a treatable cause behind some of these cases. This was mostly Delta-wave infection, and 74% of the patients had mild illness. So even milder COVID-19 may leave some people with gut symptoms, though the English study suggests the risk is much lower than after hospitalisation. The authors say this problem tends to improve over time. Who Should Be Most Careful, And What Are The Warning Signs? Looking across the studies, a clear picture forms of who needs the most attention. Higher Risk Groups People who were hospitalized with COVID-19, especially those who were very sick (English study) Older adults, especially those over 60 (English and Saudi studies) People who had gut symptoms during the infection (Saudi and Indian studies) People with IBD, particularly those on immunosuppressant medicines, who may benefit from full vaccination with boosters (Chinese study) People with existing gut disease or on blood thinners, where bleeding risk is higher (review by Cappell and Friedel) Warning Signs That Need Medical Attention Black, tarry stools or vomiting blood Fresh red blood in the stool Severe or worsening belly pain Belly pain with fever Pain or bowel changes lasting weeks that affect daily life What Should You Do Now? See a doctor if symptoms persist. Lasting stomach pain or changes in bowel habits after COVID-19 should not be ignored. A doctor can check for infections, inflammation and other health problems. Seek help if daily life is affected. Ask whether ongoing digestive problems could be linked to long COVID. Get checked after severe COVID-19. People who were hospitalised or seriously ill may need follow-up for digestive problems. Stay up to date with vaccination. Studies suggest vaccination may reduce the risk of digestive problems after COVID-19. Do not panic. Most people recover without long-term gut problems. The risk appears higher in those who had severe COVID-19. Remember: COVID-19 can affect gut health for months or even years, especially after severe infection. If digestive problems continue after recovery, consult a doctor. A quick gut-health quiz Is Your Gut Trying to Tell You Something? How much do you know about digestion, common symptoms and gut health after an infection? Try these five easy questions! Gut Health Quiz Question 1 of 5 Feeling bloated after a meal? What does bloating usually mean? Quiz complete Your Gut Health Score 0/5 Correct answers Every correct answer is a step towards better gut-health awareness. Remember: COVID-19 can affect the digestive system as well as the lungs. Persistent or concerning digestive symptoms should not be ignored. Speak to a healthcare professional for advice. This quiz is for general awareness and is not a tool for diagnosing a health condition. While the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated notable variability in disease severity—with older adults and individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic disorders experiencing increased vulnerability—traditional two-dimensional cell cultures and animal models have displayed limited capacity to accurately replicate human lung physiology. Human lung organoids have emerged as an alternative platform capable of modeling human-specific cellular architecture, host-virus interactions, and disease-relevant biological responses. Investigations highlighted in the review show that lung organoid models can replicate critical hallmarks of SARS-CoV-2 infection, such as viral replication, epithelial injury, and innate immune activation, while also serving as a flexible testbed for evaluating antiviral and host-directed therapeutics under physiologically relevant conditions. However, direct SARS-CoV-2 studies comparing lung organoids derived from younger and older donors remain limited. Current understanding of age-related mechanisms relies primarily on human tissue analyses, immune-integrated organoids, and age-stratified respiratory epithelial models rather than definitive age-stratified lung organoid experiments. Consequently, the authors conclude that while human lung organoids represent valuable mechanistic tools that strengthen the biological plausibility of epidemiological associations, translational evidence remains incomplete for donor age and several common systemic comorbidities. COVID)已成为重大公共卫生挑战,幸存者常报告持续性呼吸困难、疲劳和运动不耐受。虽然早期影像学研究聚焦于肺实质病变,但范式转变已识别出肺血管异常——特别是内皮炎(endotheliitis)、微血栓形成(microthrombosis)和适应性不良的血管新生(maladaptive angiogenesis)——是Long COVID表型的关键驱动因素。主体:该疾病的特征为"内皮炎",即病毒通过ACE2受体直接进入细胞,促发促凝血状态和原位微血栓(in situ microthrombi)形成。免疫血栓形成(immunothrombosis)涉及中性粒细胞胞外诱捕网(NETs)和具有淀粉样性质的纤维蛋白微凝块(amyloid-like fibrin microclots),后者对自然降解具有抵抗性,进一步加重了病情。此外,通过套叠性血管新生(intussusceptive angiogenesis)和"血管修剪"(vascular pruning,即远端毛细血管的丢失)进行的结构重塑减少了有效气体交换表面积。常规CT肺动脉造影(CTPA)常无法检测这些微血管变化,尽管患者表现出严重症状。然而,先进成像模态提供了更深入的见解。双能CT(DECT)揭示了即使在形态学正常的肺实质中也存在持续性楔形灌注缺损。定量CT(QCT)允许测量"血管修剪",显示小血管体积(PBV5)显著减少。超极化氙-129 MRI(Hp-XeMRI)识别出标志性的红细胞(RBC):屏障缺陷,表明从肺泡到红细胞的气体转移受损——这一发现即使在标准CT和肺功能检查正常时也持续存在。V/Q SPECT和相位分辨功能肺(PREFUL)MRI等功能性技术进一步证实了指示弥漫性小血管病变的"斑驳"灌注模式。简要结论:本综述强调Long COVID涉及独特的血管表型,需要功能和定量影像学以实现准确诊断。遵循2025年国际共识指南——建议感染后3个月进行影像学检查并采用配对吸气/呼气方案——对于标准化诊疗和区分血管性与气道相关症状至关重要。 背景 点击获取iPSC技术服务(重编程、基因编辑和定向分化)的详细资料领 取 由严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)引起的新型冠状病毒疾病2019(COVID-19)已从急性大流行病演变为慢性公共卫生挑战,其特征为初始病毒清除后症状的长期持续。2020年5月,意大利患者Elisa Perego创造了"Long-COVID-19"标签来描述其 COVID-19 症状在康复后长期持续的经历。该综合征有多种命名,包括SARS-CoV-2急性期后遗症、Long COVID或COVID-19后状况,影响相当比例的幸存者,表现为咳嗽、持续性疲劳、劳力后不适、呼吸困难、运动不耐受和胸痛等一系列衰弱症状。尽管早期影像学研究自然优先关注该疾病显著的肺实质后遗症(如磨玻璃影、纤维化样改变、支气管扩张、小叶间隔增厚、网状影和实变),但对疾病病理生理学的理解已发生范式转变。目前日益认识到SARS-CoV-2不仅是呼吸道病原体,更是强效血管侵袭因子,肺血管异常构成Long COVID的独特且关键的表型。研究人员呈现一篇叙述性综述,整合了常规影像学、先进功能模态和新兴定量技术的已发表数据,以构建急性期后肺血管功能障碍的综合模型。综述整合了双能计算机断层扫描(DECT)、微血管定量CT(QCT)、超极化气体磁共振成像(MRI)和通气/灌注(V/Q)单光子发射计算机断层扫描(SPECT)的报告,以详述Long COVID中血管异常的病理生理学。此外,研究人员审查了最新的多学会影像监测和报告共识指南,为这一复杂患者群体的放射学管理提供了稳健框架。 血管损伤的病理生理机制 内皮-病毒界面与内皮炎 血管内皮作为体循环与肺实质之间的主要界面。SARS-CoV-2主要通过血管紧张素转换酶2(ACE2)受体进入宿主细胞,该受体广泛表达于肺内皮细胞表面。这些细胞的直接病毒感染促发一系列内皮炎症反应,称为"内皮炎",是疾病血管表现的核心驱动因素。在稳态条件下,内皮维持抗血栓和抗炎表面。病毒介导的损伤打破这一平衡,导致糖萼脱落、内皮下基质暴露以及促血栓因子如血管性血友病因子(vWF)的释放。这种向促凝血状态的转变促进了肺微血管内原位血栓的形成,这一过程不同于起源于深静脉血栓形成(DVT)的经典血栓栓塞。影像学研究已将这种内皮功能障碍与D-二聚体、纤维蛋白原和C反应蛋白(CRP)等生物标志物的持续升高相关联,即使在急性感染消退数月后仍然存在。这些标志物的持续存在表明内皮炎可能并非仅限于急性期的短暂现象,而是Long COVID中一个迁延的慢性过程,持续刺激血管炎症和功能障碍。 免疫血栓形成与微凝块形成 COVID-19凝血病的定义性特征是"免疫血栓形成",即免疫系统激活凝血级联以捕获病原体的机制。在此过程中,中性粒细胞释放中性粒细胞胞外诱捕网(NETs)——由DNA和组蛋白组成的网状结构——捕获病毒,但同时也作为血小板聚集和血栓形成的支架。近期利用荧光显微镜和流式细胞术的研究已识别出Long COVID患者血浆中存在持续性淀粉样纤维蛋白微凝块。与正常纤维蛋白凝块不同,这些淀粉样结构对纤维蛋白溶解具有抵抗性,并包裹各种促炎分子,包括α-2抗纤溶酶,进一步抑制凝块分解。虽然这些微凝块低于标准CT成像的分辨率,但它们为解释DECT上观察到的灌注缺损和超极化氙-129 MRI(Hp-XeMRI)上见到的气体转移异常提供了必要的生物学背景。它们代表了"微观"阻塞表现为"宏观"功能损害。这些微凝块的检测与"脑雾"和疲劳症状密切相关,提示包括肺循环在内的系统性微血管病变。 血管新生与血管重塑 在初始血管损伤后,肺血管系统试图通过血管新生进行修复。然而,在COVID-19背景下,这一修复过程常失调。重症COVID-19患者肺组织的组织病理学分析揭示了套叠性血管新生(IA)的高患病率。与通过内皮芽生形成新血管的 sprouting angiogenesis(SA)不同,IA涉及通过形成经腔支柱将现有血管腔分裂为二。虽然IA允许血管床快速扩张,但由此产生的网络常扭曲且血流动力学效率低下。重塑改变了肺血管阻力并导致影像学上检测到的V/Q失调。此外,有证据表明小毛细血管的选择性丢失,通常称为"血管修剪",本质上减少了可用于气体交换的血管床横截面积。这种结构性丢失迫使血流进入较大、低阻力的血管,形成可在CT上定量的血流重分布模式。 常规计算机断层扫描(CT)与血管造影 高分辨率CT(HRCT)和CT肺动脉造影(CTPA)是胸部影像学的核心工具。在Long COVID的评估中,其作用已从单纯排除急性病变演变为识别慢性血管疾病的细微征象。 肺动脉高压 COVID-19后肺动脉高压(PAH)的发展存在争议但有可能。提出的机制包括氧化应激、线粒体功能障碍、DNA损伤、炎症、缺氧、内皮功能障碍和肺微栓塞。此类PH被认为是第3组PH(由纤维化和/或阻塞性肺疾病引起)和第4组PH(由肺动脉阻塞引起)的混合型。一项住院患者的早期研究报告PH患病率约为13%。CT上描绘的肺动脉高压特征包括"中央肺动脉扩张、段和亚段动脉口径突然减小、右心增大、心包积液以及肺实质斑驳衰减模式"。 慢性血栓栓塞后遗症 初始感染期间急性肺栓塞(PE)的高发病率引发了对幸存者发展为慢性血栓栓塞性肺动脉高压(CTEPH)或慢性血栓栓塞性肺疾病(CTEPD)的担忧。总体而言,虽然急性PE随访病例中明显的CTEPH相对罕见(累积2年发病率估计约2.3%),但残留血栓物质的患病率更高。 尽管存在这些已知实体,Long COVID中的一个重大挑战是许多患者表现为严重呼吸困难和运动不耐受,但CTPA扫描对大血栓呈"阴性"。这一差异凸显了常规CTPA在检测微血管疾病方面的局限性,并需要使用功能或定量影像学。 斑驳衰减:区分血管性与气道疾病 Long COVID胸部CT上最常见且最令人困惑的发现之一是斑驳衰减——不同肺密度的斑片状模式。该模式可由三种主要病因引起:浸润性肺疾病、小气道疾病(空气潴留)或闭塞性血管疾病(斑驳灌注)。区分这些病因对患者管理至关重要。 斑驳灌注(血管病因) 在此模式中,较低衰减区域代表灌注减少(少血)区域。这些透亮区域内的血管口径通常小于密度较高、灌注较好肺区的血管。这反映了血流从阻塞或血管收缩的血管向正常血管的重新分布。在Long COVID中,这通常是上述微血栓形成或血管修剪的表现。斑驳灌注的诊断依赖特定的放射学标准:首先,透亮区域显示肺血管口径较邻近较高衰减区域减小,表明为血管性而非气道性病因。此外,透亮区与致密区之间的衰减梯度通常在呼气成像上评估以排除主要的小气道贡献。需要认识到斑驳灌注和气道疾病引起的斑驳衰减可以共存,特别是在血管和气道病理均普遍存在的Long COVID患者中。 空气潴留(气道病因) 小气道疾病,如感染后细支气管炎,也可引起斑驳衰减。在此情况下,呼气时空气无法从肺泡排出,使受累肺过度充气且透亮。为将其与血管性斑驳区分,配对吸气和呼气CT采集至关重要。近期使用配对CT方案在Long COVID队列中的研究发现空气潴留患病率极高,高达77%的有症状患者。这表明小气道疾病是Long COVID的主要组成部分,可能与血管异常共存。 支气管动脉肥大 支气管动脉为肺组织提供体循环动脉血。正常情况下它们较小(<1.5 mm),在CT上常难以显示。然而,在慢性肺血管阻塞——如CTEPH或弥漫性微血管闭塞——的情况下,支气管循环肥大以向缺血肺实质提供侧支血流。在Long COVID背景下,支气管动脉肥大(定义为直径>2 mm)作为慢性肺血管受损的强效间接标志物。有证据表明在无既往基础肺疾病的情况下存在支气管动脉肥大或肺分流。这些分流可能是COVID-19相关微栓塞事件的结果。 肺动脉假性动脉瘤 有证据支持COVID-19与"血管炎性过程如肺血管炎、川崎病和皮肤血管炎"的关联。假性动脉瘤的发展可发生于急性重症COVID-19感染期间或亚急性至延迟表现。许多Long COVID患者具有糖尿病、高龄、移植后或接受化疗或免疫抑制等合并症。这些条件也使其易患侵袭性感染,其中最暴发性的为肺毛霉病。肺毛霉病本身使患者易发生肺动脉假性动脉瘤。 定量CT(QCT):血管修剪 肺血容量(PBV)分布的定量分析,称为"血管修剪"评估,使用自动化软件分割肺血管树并根据横截面积(CSA)对血管进行分类。多项研究报告Long COVID患者,特别是急性期住院的患者,与健康对照相比PBV5和PBV5/总血容量比值显著降低。远端血管系统的这种"修剪"意味着毛细血管床的丢失或广泛的血管收缩。同时,PBV10常增加,代表因远端阻力增加而导致的近端血管代偿性扩张。血管修剪的临床意义:血管修剪程度(较低的PBV5)已独立地与弥散功能(DLCO)降低和运动耐量下降相关,即使在肺实质阴影极少的患者中也是如此。这确立了血管修剪作为功能障碍的形态学生物标志物。有趣的是,一些非住院Long COVID患者的研究显示CT上修剪不如住院队列明显,提示较轻病例中的微血管损伤可能是功能性的(因此仅在MRI/SPECT上可见)而非结构性的。 先进功能成像:双能CT(DECT) 双能CT(DECT)已成为评估Long COVID的关键问题解决工具。通过在两个不同能量谱(如80 kVp和140 kVp)采集数据,DECT允许组织材料分解。这一能力使得生成碘密度图成为可能,提供肺实质灌注(PBV图)的直接可视化以及标准形态学图像。灌注缺损的患病率与特征:DECT研究揭示了Long COVID患者肺灌注缺损(PDs)的高患病率,通常在CTPA图像上无可见血栓。灌注异常存在于相当比例的有症状患者中,各队列报告率从36%至60%以上不等。这些缺损通常为段或亚段性,常呈楔形。与急性PE的离散充盈缺损不同,Long COVID中的PDs常反映下游微血管闭塞或毛细血管破坏。虽然PDs常见于残留肺实质阴影(如磨玻璃或纤维化)区域(由于缺氧性血管收缩),但一个关键发现是形态学正常肺实质中存在PDs。这一发现强烈支持原发性血管病理(如内皮炎或微血栓形成)而非纯粹继发性血管收缩的假说。因此,DECT可能有助于阐明COVID-19肺炎的病理生理学。灌注异常的纵向演变:这些灌注缺损的持续性是Long COVID的关键特征。纵向DECT研究已追踪患者从急性期到急性期后恢复期。3个月间隔:一项44例患者的研究显示16例(36.3%)在平均83天随访时保留灌注缺损。重要的是,这些患者初始D-二聚体和CRP水平显著较高,将急性炎症负荷与慢性血管功能障碍联系起来。1年间隔:虽然许多灌注缺损随时间消退,但已有记录持续长达12个月,特别是在重症急性病患者中。这种长期持续性提示在某些个体中血管重塑是不可逆的或缓慢消退的。临床与生物标志物相关性:DECT上PDs的存在不仅仅是影像学异常,还与临床严重程度相关。持续性PDs患者表现出更高的持续症状如呼吸困难和疲劳的发生率。此外,统计分析显示初始CT严重度评分和入院D-二聚体水平可预测晚期灌注缺损的发展。这确立了DECT作为有价值的预后工具,能够识别有Long COVID相关血管病变风险的患者。先前一项研究发现"在13%的截断值时,DECT评分预测重症疾病的敏感性为100%,特异性为77%,表明DECT在筛查COVID-19肺炎个体时比其他检测更敏感"。治疗策略:俯卧位通气已被证明可显著降低插管COVID-19肺炎患者的死亡率。DECT上的灌注分布可指导体位策略;在背侧血流减少的病例中,俯卧位通气被发现有效。 Long COVID中的对比剂与非对比剂肺MRI 超极化氙-129 MRI(Hp-XeMRI) 或许检测Long COVID细微生理紊乱最敏感的模态是超极化氙-129 MRI(Hp-XeMRI)。该技术利用氙气的独特性质,吸入后溶解于肺组织并进入肺毛细血管血液,允许对三个不同 compartment 进行独立成像。RBC:屏障缺陷:Hp-XeMRI在Long COVID中的标志性发现是RBC:Barrier比值的显著降低。该指标代表从肺泡膜到红细胞的气体转移效率。RBC:Barrier比值降低意味着虽然气体能到达肺泡并穿过进入间质(屏障),但遇到阻止其与血红蛋白结合的阻滞。该阻滞归因于微血管闭塞(微血栓形成)、毛细血管减少(修剪)或弥散屏障增厚(尽管纤维化通常也会增加屏障信号)。关键的是,该缺陷已在CT扫描正常且肺功能检查(PFTs)正常或接近正常的患者中观察到。在一项标志性研究中,从未住院的Long COVID患者表现出与对照相比显著较低的RBC:Barrier比值,尽管CT上无可见肺损伤。MRI可能比CT对微血管问题更敏感或更有针对性,因为它直接检查肺泡-毛细血管边界的功能。氙转移缺陷的幅度与呼吸困难及运动不耐受的临床指标相关。该模态本质上可视化了Long COVID患者中表现为严重症状但标准检查"正常"的"缺失环节"。它证实病理位于肺泡-毛细血管界面,这是常规成像无法触及的区域。 PREFUL MRI 一种评估肺功能的新方法称为相位分辨功能肺(PREFUL)MRI,利用自由呼吸期间内源性肺氢质子信号的变化作为通气和灌注异常的替代指标。先前研究表明动态对比增强(DCE)MRI和超极化129Xe MRI与PREFUL MRI评估的灌注缺损百分比(缩写为QDP)和通气缺损百分比(VDP)具有良好的相关性。PREFUL MRI是Long COVID患者长期监测的非常适合工具,因为它可以在自由呼吸时进行,不需要对比剂,采集仅需几分钟(每个层面约一分钟)。PREFUL MRI先前已证明VDP从急性期到6个月随访显著下降,不再与健康对照有差异。然而,QDP在一年随访时仍远高于健康对照,提示灌注异常在初始感染后很长时间内持续存在。研究表明QDP受Long COVID存在(高于健康个体)、住院状态(住院者更高)和性别(男性高于女性)的影响。在研究人员所在机构,Long COVID患者在CT不确定时接受PREFUL MRI检查,作为另一项比较PREFUL MRI和动态对比增强MRI的研究的一部分。 动态对比增强肺MRI DECT、SPECT/CT、DCE-MRI和肺动脉造影均可用于研究肺内血流。DCE-MRI区别于早期技术的主要优势在于其能以良好分辨率产生空间和时间信息,使得识别小灌注缺损和可能的分流成为可能。作为脑灌注成像的临床常用技术,DCE-MRI也已有效应用于肺部疾病如囊性纤维化、肺栓塞、肺动脉(PA)狭窄、肺血管炎和慢性阻塞性肺疾病。该模态可评估的参数包括相对肺血容量(rPBV)、相对肺血流量(rPBF)、平均通过时间(MTT)、达峰时间(TTP)和TTP比值。TTP和TTP比值代表总肺灌注阻力和灌注延迟的肺比例。COVID后呼吸困难的男性在DCE-MRI上显示对比剂团注到达延迟,这可能指示原发性血管病变或缺氧性血管收缩的后续后果。这些结果暗示驱动COVID后呼吸困难的机制存在性别差异,因为这一效应在女性患者中未一致观察到,PREFUL MRI也是如此。已有报道急性COVID-19病理生理学中的性别差异,男性因COVID-19相关呼吸衰竭的死亡率更高。这可能与"血管紧张素转换酶II受体表达较高、性激素的免疫调节、年龄和X连锁基因表达等原因"有关。在住院COVID-19男性患者中,急性疾病严重程度与随访MRI时灌注通过时间延长相关。 通气/灌注(V/Q)SPECT 核医学技术,特别是V/Q SPECT/CT,提供了另一种评估肺血管功能的稳健方法。通过使用灌注放射性示踪剂,通常为锝-99m大颗粒白蛋白(Tc-99m MAA)和单独的通气示踪剂(如Technegas),V/Q SPECT可以高灵敏度地识别不匹配。COVID后患者的V/Q SPECT分析通常产生三种不同模式:匹配缺损:通气和灌注均减少的区域。这对应于肺实质瘢痕、肺不张或发生缺氧性血管收缩的严重磨玻璃影。这在COVID-19后残留肺异常患者中常见。不匹配缺损(血管表型):通气保留而灌注缺失或减少的区域。该模式是肺栓塞的经典征象。然而,在Long COVID中,即使无中央凝块,也常见广泛的、斑片状的、非段性不匹配缺损。这种"斑驳"灌注模式指示弥漫性微血管血栓形成或小血管病变。反向不匹配:罕见情况下,磨玻璃影区域可能显示相对于通气增加的灌注("奢侈灌注")。存在"炎症区域正常生理性缺氧血管收缩的丧失,导致该区域血管扩张和血液可能从无炎症区域分流"。对微血管疾病优于CTPA:比较研究表明V/Q SPECT在检测慢性远端血栓栓塞疾病方面可能优于CTPA。"斑驳"模式与QCT上见到的"修剪"和Hp-XeMRI上见到的"RBC缺陷"具有相似的潜在病理生理基础。 共识指南与报告标准化 认识到Long COVID影像实践和报告术语的异质性,北美放射学会(RSNA)、胸部放射学会(STR)和欧洲胸部影像学会(ESTI)于2025年发布了多学会共识声明以标准化诊疗。成像指征与时机:共识专家组(RSNA/STR/ESTI)推荐了Long COVID患者成像的具体标准:主要指征:对于初始感染后3个月持续或加重的呼吸道症状患者,且这些症状已持续至少2个月且不能用其他原因(如心力衰竭)解释,推荐胸部CT。急性变化:对于呼吸状态急性恶化的患者,建议使用标准剂量CT(而非低剂量)以排除PE等急性并发症。住院队列:对于需要住院的中重度急性COVID-19患者,无论症状如何,3-6个月随访CT被认为是适当的,因为残留异常患病率高。采集方案:在遵循辐射安全原则(ALARA)的同时最大化诊断收益,指南建议:方案:低剂量薄层(≤1.5 mm)非增强CT是监测的标准。血管评估:如果非增强CT发现不能完全解释患者症状(如严重呼吸困难伴极少纤维化),强烈推荐增强CTPA。这允许评估CTEPH和血管口径。呼气成像:明确推荐包含配对吸气和呼气采集以评估空气潴留,这是呼吸困难病因的关键鉴别因素。标准化术语:共识的关键组成部分是语言标准化以防止诊断混淆。"COVID-19后残留肺异常":这是持续性发现的首选术语,如RSNA/STR/ESTI共识声明所推荐。该术语区别于Fleischner学会或MeSH术语,由多学会专家组专门创造以描述COVID-19后肺实质后遗症,同时避免与进展性纤维化疾病的预后混淆。避免"间质性肺异常(ILA)":专家组明确建议不要对COVID后发现使用"ILA"术语,因为COVID后残留CT异常不是偶然发现的。ILA通常指可能进展为纤维化的临床前间质性肺疾病(如特发性肺纤维化—IPF)。相比之下,COVID后异常通常随时间消退或稳定,类似于SARS 2003感染。使用"ILA"可能导致不适当的预后判断和管理。学会建议尽可能与COVID前CT扫描比较以"评估已知既往纤维化间质性肺疾病(ILD)的进展"。职业暴露史也可能有助于区分COVID后变化与既往职业暴露引起的变化。Fleischner学会术语:敦促放射科医生严格遵循Fleischner学会词汇表描述发现(如磨玻璃、网状、牵拉性支气管扩张)以确保跨机构一致性。 鉴别诊断与类似病变 Long COVID中肺血管疾病的放射学征象并非特异性的,与其他血管和间质性病变有共同特征。细致的鉴别诊断至关重要。慢性血栓栓塞性肺动脉高压(CTEPH):经典CTEPH表现为机化性偏心血栓和血管网。虽然Long COVID可导致CTEPH,但Long COVID中的血管发现通常比经典CTEPH中见到的近端、可手术治疗的疾病更细微和远端(微血管性)。支气管动脉肥大在两者中均常见,但严重右心室劳损在典型Long COVID患者中较晚期CTEPH少见。肺动脉高压(PAH):特发性PAH表现为中央肺动脉扩张和外周修剪("螺旋状血管")。仅凭CT将其与COVID后修剪区分可能具有挑战性。任何原因PH中的灌注缺损均为异质性和斑片状。此外,特发性PAH中的灌注缺损比CTEPH更小且边界不清。另一方面,COVID中灌注缺损的形态按频率递减依次分类为无定形斑驳状(如特发性或慢性血栓栓塞性肺动脉高压中所见)和楔形(类似于急性肺栓塞患者中所见的表现)。过敏性肺炎(HP):欧洲呼吸学会/美国胸科学会(ERS/ATS)2025年更新的间质性肺炎国际多学科分类引入了"细支气管中心性间质性肺炎(BIP)"术语作为以前与HP相关的以气道为中心的间质性肺炎的形态学模式描述词。当确认对已知吸入抗原的免疫介导反应时,HP仍是既定的临床诊断;然而,当未识别暴露时,形态学模式现分类为"特发性BIP"。此外,HP现分类为非纤维化型与纤维化型,取代了以前的急性/亚急性/慢性分类。HP是斑驳衰减的经典原因。与Long COVID一样,它显示磨玻璃影和空气潴留;两者结合产生三密度模式。将HP与Long COVID区分主要依赖临床病史(抗原暴露 vs. 病毒感染)和纤维化的特定分布(HP中常为上/中区和支气管血管周围 vs. COVID中为外周/基底)。此外,HP中的磨玻璃影(GGOs)边界不清,呼气扫描上有空气潴留。局限性:应承认本综述的若干局限性。首先,研究人员的示例病例中缺乏某些纵向和比较影像学。具体而言,数据库中无法提供展示V/Q SPECT阳性而CTPA阴性的配对病例。此外,部分患者缺乏基线COVID前影像学(如图1)和急性期影像学(如图3);因此,虽然放射学发现基于时间表现临床归因于COVID后后遗症,但无明确基线相关性时不能完全排除既往心肺疾病或替代演变途径。其次,作为叙述性综述,本文受文献选择偏倚的固有影响。第三,虽然Hp-XeMRI和PREFUL MRI等先进功能模态为微血管功能障碍提供了深刻的病理生理学见解,但其可用性目前主要限于专业研究中心,限制了广泛的临床验证。最后,Long COVID仍是一个快速发展的领域;诊断术语和成像时间点的标准化依赖于近期共识指南,尚待长期、大规模纵向验证。 结论 Long COVID以独特的肺血管表型为特征——由内皮炎、微血栓形成和适应性不良的血管新生驱动——在常规CTPA上常无法检测。先进功能和定量模态,包括DECT、Hp-XeMRI、QCT和V/Q SPECT,对于识别这些微血管紊乱和弥合有症状患者与"正常"标准检查之间的差距至关重要。遵循2025年RSNA/STR/ESTI共识指南,特别是在成像时机、配对吸气/呼气方案以及使用标准化术语如"COVID-19后残留肺异常"方面,对于确保诊断一致性和指导这一复杂患者群体的血管中心管理策略至关重要。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 records.content_title: Shoulder Injury Rare but More Common After COVID-19 Than Flu Shots
records.content: Although rare, the absolute risk of shoulder injury related to vaccine administration (SIRVA) after COVID-19 or flu vaccination should be considered alongside the established benefits of both vaccines, according to a recent study published in JAMA Internal Medicine.1 Adverse events or injection site reactions are not uncommon from vaccines. SIRVA was added to the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program vaccine injury table in 2017 based on accumulating case series. Epidemiological studies of SIRVA have been limited because the condition lacks specific diagnostic codes, is rare, must be distinguished from transient postvaccination reactions, and its long-term prognosis remains poorly characterized. Prior case reports and surveillance studies have noted instances of SIRVA after COVID-19 vaccination; however, they could not quantify its incidence relative to other routinely administered vaccines. In 2024, the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine identified this as an important evidence gap.1 Comparing SIRVA Risk Across More Than 1.8 Million Vaccinations The retrospective cohort study was conducted at Kaiser Permanente Southern California (KPSC), an integrated health care system whose prepaid model captures member data, including sociodemographics, encounters, diagnoses, laboratory tests, pharmacy use, and vaccinations. KPSC members 18 years or older who received a COVID-19 or flu vaccine between August 1, 2023, and April 30, 2024, were included in the analysis. A SIRVA case was defined by 5 required criteria: anatomical concordance with the vaccination arm, symptom onset within 7 days of vaccination, symptom duration greater than 30 days to exclude transient reactogenicity events, vaccination identified as a possible cause, and no other identifiable causes for the shoulder condition. There were 1,366,362 individuals who met the criteria for the study across 1,901,588 vaccinations. The mean age was 58.4 years, and 782,994 (57.3%) were female individuals. Among eligible vaccinations, 313,571 (16.5%) were received by Asian or other Pacific Islander individuals; 134,951 (7.1%) by Black individuals; 704,502 (37.0%) by Hispanic individuals; 667,597 (35.1%) by White individuals; and 80,967 (4.3%) by individuals of multiple, other, or unknown race and ethnicity. Of the eligible vaccinations, 70,952 (3.7%) were simultaneous COVID-19 and influenza vaccinations and therefore were excluded from the primary analysis. Overall, the final analysis included 1,830,636 vaccinations, of which 1,234,022 were for the flu and 596,614 were for COVID-19. Of the COVID-19 vaccines, 99.98% were Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA. Of the flu vaccines, 66.40% were standard-dose inactivated quadrivalent influenza vaccine (SD-IIV4), and 33.58% were high-dose inactivated quadrivalent influenza vaccine (HD-IIV4). In a CDC survey of more than 12,500 people who received a third dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna vaccine, 79.4% reported local injection site reactions like itching or redness and 74.1% reported systemic reactions like fatigue, muscle aches, and headaches. Systemic reactions mostly occurred the day after receiving the shot.2 These findings show how common short-term reactions are after COVID-19 vaccination, which the SIRVA case definition excluded by requiring symptoms to last more than 30 days. SIRVA Incidence Higher After COVID-19 Vaccination Researchers identified 252 SIRVA cases: 110 after a COVID-19 vaccination and 142 after a flu vaccination. SIRVA incidence was 1.84 per 10,000 COVID-19 vaccinations compared with 1.15 per 10,000 flu vaccinations (adjusted relative risk [aRR], 1.63; 95% CI, 1.16-2.28), or approximately 7 additional cases per 100,000 vaccinations. SIRVA incidence increased with age after both vaccines. However, among adults 65 years or older, SIRVA risk did not differ significantly between COVID-19 vaccination and HD-IIV4, a recommended influenza vaccine for this age group (aRR, 1.41; 95% CI, 0.92-2.15). COVID-19 vaccination was associated with a significantly higher risk than SD-IIV4 in older adults, but that comparison was based on only 9 SIRVA cases after SD-IIV4. Furthermore, the median time to the first shoulder-related encounter was 46 days after influenza vaccination and 51.5 days after COVID-19 vaccination, even though 94.7% of confirmed cases had symptom onset within 2 days of vaccination. The study had several limitations. Case identification relied on patients seeking care and on clinical documentation, which may underestimate true SIRVA incidence. Its observational design limits causal inference, and residual confounding from unmeasured factors, such as needle length, injection site within the deltoid, or undiagnosed shoulder conditions, may persist. Also, results from a single health system using mostly Pfizer-BioNTech doses during 1 season may not be generalizable. "Despite the higher incidence after COVID-19 vaccination, the benefits of COVID-19 and influenza vaccination in preventing severe disease and hospitalization may outweigh the small absolute and relative risks of SIRVA," the study authors wrote.1 References 1. Zheng C, Qian L, Sy LS, et al. Risk of shoulder injury related to vaccine administration for COVID-19 and influenza vaccinations. JAMA Intern Med. Published online November 4, 2026. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2026.5899 2. records.content_title: Health Canada Authorizes Moderna's mRNA Influenza and Combination Influenza and COVID-19 Vaccines
records.content: Canada becomes the first country to authorize both Moderna’s mRNA seasonal influenza vaccine, mFLUSIVA ® , and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine, mCOFLU ® CAMBRIDGE, MA / ACCESS Newswire / November 5, 2026 / Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today announced that Health Canada has authorized mFLUSIVA ® (Influenza mRNA vaccine; mRNA-1010) and mCOFLU ® (Combined Influenza and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine; mRNA-1083) for adults 50 years of age and older. Canada is the first country in the world to authorize both Moderna’s seasonal mRNA influenza vaccine and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine. “Health Canada’s authorizations of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU today mark another important step in bringing the benefits of mRNA technology to seasonal respiratory vaccination. It’s not every day that a company gets two product approvals on the same day,” said Stéphane Bancel, Chief Executive Officer of Moderna. “Influenza and COVID-19 continue to place a significant burden on public health, particularly among older adults. These milestones reflect our commitment to advancing innovative vaccine options that help protect Canadians and support more resilient health systems.” mFLUSIVA is Canada’s first mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, while mCOFLU is the country’s first combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine. Health Canada’s authorizations follow the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s approval of mFLUSIVA in August 2026 and the European Commission’s authorization of the Company’s combination influenza and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, marketed as mCOMBRIAX®, in April 2026. Both vaccines remain under regulatory review in additional markets. mFLUSIVA is authorized for active immunization of adults 50 years of age and older for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus subtypes A and B represented in the vaccine. i mCOFLU is authorized for active immunization of adults 50 years of age and older for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus types A and B represented in the vaccine and SARS-CoV-2. ii Health Canada’s authorization of mFLUSIVA is supported by the pivotal Phase 3 mRNA-1010-P304 study (NCT06602024), a randomized, active-controlled trial involving approximately 40,800 adults 50 years of age and older across 11 countries. mFLUSIVA met all pre-specified statistical success criteria, including the highest level of pre-specified superiority, demonstrating relative vaccine efficacy of 26.6% (95% CI: 16.7-35.4) in adults 50 years of age and older and 27.4% (95% CI: 12.1-40.0) in adults 65 years of age and older compared with a standard-dose inactivated influenza vaccine against RT-PCR-confirmed, protocol-defined influenza-like illness caused by influenza A or B. iii The authorization is also supported by the Phase 3 mRNA-1010-P303 Part C study (NCT05827978), which demonstrated superior antibody responses compared with a high-dose inactivated influenza vaccine in adults 65 years of age and older. iv Across both studies, the most commonly reported adverse reactions included injection-site pain, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, chills and axillary (underarm) swelling or tenderness. Most solicited reactions were mild to moderate and resolved within one to two days. v mCOFLU builds on the clinical development of mFLUSIVA and mNEXSPIKE ® . Health Canada’s authorization of mCOFLU is supported by a pivotal Phase 3 trial (NCT06097273), a randomized, observer-blind, active-controlled study evaluating safety, reactogenicity and immunogenicity in two cohorts of approximately 4,000 adults each. Adults 65 years of age and older received mCOFLU or co-administered Fluzone HD ® , a high-dose influenza vaccine, and Spikevax ® , Moderna’s licensed COVID-19 vaccine. Adults 50 to 64 years of age received mCOFLU or co-administered Fluarix ® , a standard-dose influenza vaccine, and Spikevax. vi The study met all primary endpoints demonstrating non-inferiority of immune responses. Following a single dose, mCOFLU elicited statistically significantly higher immune responses against three influenza strains (A/H1N1, A/H3N2 and B/Victoria) and SARS-CoV-2 in both age cohorts compared with co-administered licensed comparator vaccines. The exception was B/Yamagata, a strain no longer recommended for inclusion in seasonal influenza vaccines, for which a statistically significantly higher immune response was not observed in adults 65 years of age and older. vii mCOFLU demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile. The most commonly reported adverse reactions included injection-site pain, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, joint pain, chills and axillary (underarm) swelling or tenderness. Most were mild to moderate and short in duration. No serious adverse events were assessed as related to mCOFLU in the pivotal study. viii Moderna will engage with Canadian health authorities and immunization partners as it advances plans for the future availability of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU in Canada. About Moderna Moderna is a pioneer and leader in the field of mRNA medicine. Through the advancement of its technology platform, Moderna is reimagining how medicines are made to transform how we treat and prevent diseases. Since its founding, Moderna’s mRNA platform has enabled the development of vaccines and therapeutics across infectious diseases, cancer, rare diseases and more. With a global team and a unique culture, driven by the company’s values and mindsets, Moderna’s mission is to deliver the greatest possible impact to people through mRNA medicines. For more information about Moderna, please visit modernatx.com and connect with us on X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and LinkedIn. mFLUSIVA ® , mCOFLU ® , Spikevax ® , mCOMBRIAX ® and mNEXSPIKE ® are registered trademarks of Moderna. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended, including regarding: Moderna’s engagement with Canadian health authorities and immunization partners; the future availability of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU in Canada; the potential of Moderna’s mRNA platform to advance respiratory disease prevention; and the review of additional regulatory applications of Moderna’s influenza and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccines in other markets. The forward-looking statements in this press release are neither promises nor guarantees, and you should not place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements because they involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors, many of which are beyond Moderna’s control and which could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by these forward-looking statements. These risks, uncertainties, and other factors include those other risks and uncertainties described under the heading “Risk Factors” in Moderna’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and in subsequent filings made by Moderna with the SEC, which are available on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov . This week in Other Barks & Bites: The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has sworn in former counsel to Judge Pauline Newman as Solicitor; Reuters reports that this week’s massive tech selloff could delay the anticipated initial public offering of Anthropic stock; the Western District of Washington releases an unredacted version of the Federal Trade Commission’s complaint over Amazon’s covert price shifting for ad auctions; a Government Accountability Office Report shows that backlog reduction efforts at the USPTO are contributing to patent examiner attrition, in turn making agency goals unsustainable; Circuit Judge Kurt Engelhardt argues that a Fifth Circuit majority misconstrued several likelihood of confusion factors in reversing a district court ruling against Casa Azul’s trademark infringement claims; the Second Circuit affirms a $4 million statutory damages award over a luxury good reseller’s sale of counterfeit Chanel goods not found in the company’s internal inventory database; the Federal Circuit hears oral arguments on Moderna’s government-supplier defense in a patent infringement case brought over its COVID-19 vaccine; and the Copyright Office extends the deadline for initial comments responding to its notice of inquiry on music streaming fraud to mid-December. Bites Greg Dolin Sworn in as USPTO Solicitor – Greg Dolin, former attorney with the New Civil Liberties Alliance (NCLA), where he served as counsel to Judge Pauline Newman in her battle against U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit Chief Judge Kimberly Moore, has been sworn in as the new U.S. Patent and Trademark Office Solicitor, according to IPWatchdog sources. The role would mean Dolin is in charge of representing the Office at the CAFC, which he actively challenged on behalf of Newman during his tenure as Senior Litigation Counsel with the NCLA. Following that role, Dolin joined the Department of Justice (DOJ) as Senior Counsel in the Civil Rights Division. He is also a Professor of Law at the University of Baltimore, where he has been on the faculty since 2011. Dolin has also served as clerk to Judge Newman and as Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Palau. GAO Report Says USPTO Backlog Reduction Efforts Creating Unsustainable Examiner Attrition – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) issued a report requested by Representatives Jamie Raskin (D-MD) and Hank Johnson, Jr. (D-GA) into efforts at the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office to reduce the backlog of unexamined U.S. patent applications from the January 2025 high mark of 838,000 patent applications down to a stated goal of 599,000. According to USPTO data and survey feedback, the GAO’s report found that the agency’s backlog reduction goal is unsustainable due to current high levels of attrition among the agency’s patent examiner workforce, which itself is being caused due to workplace strain from increased examiner workloads, the adoption of AI tools that are currently ineffective for prior art searching, reductions in patent examiner training and less flexible remote work policies. CAFC Mulls Moderna’s Government-Supplier Defense on COVID-19 Vaccine Appeal – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit heard oral arguments in COVID-19 vaccine developer Moderna’s appeal from a ruling by the District of Delaware that it was not immune from patent infringement liability over claims asserted by rival vaccine developers Arbutus and Genevant to a share of royalties from the sale of the COVID vaccine Spikevax. Questioning from the Federal Circuit panel, including Circuit Judges Richard Taranto and Jimmie Reyna, focused on Moderna’s defense that its vaccine shots were made for the U.S. federal government and thus the government should stand in as the defendant in the patent infringement proceedings, a position backed by the U.S. government in briefing during the Delaware district court proceedings. Unredacted FTC Complaint Alleges Amazon Covertly Raising Ad Prices By 250% – On Thursday, November 5, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced that the agency had recently filed an updated version of a complaint filed in the Western District of Washington against e-commerce giant Amazon along with attorneys general (AGs) or consumer protection divisions from 22 states over Amazon’s alleged use of deceptive and unfair practices to secretly inflate prices for its online search advertising auctions. Among the unredacted allegations are included Amazon’s secret raising of auction prices by 50% on normal auction days up to as much as 250% on major holidays like Black Friday or Prime Day, with some advertisers experiencing average cost-per-click increases of over 200% during the 2021 holiday season. Circuit Judge Engelhardt Dissents From Fifth Circuit Vacatur in Casa Azul Trademark Case – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit issued a ruling in Casa Tradición S.A. de C.V .v. Casa Azul Spirits, L.L.C. in which a panel majority vacated the Southern District of Texas’ judgment that Casa Azul failed to show a likelihood of confusion between its own tequila product and Casa Tradición’s “CLASE AZUL”-branded tequila after the appellate court found clear error in the district court’s analysis of several likelihood of confusion marks, including that “CLASE AZUL” was suggestive rather than descriptive. Writing in partial dissent was Circuit Judge Kurt Engelhardt who would affirm the district court’s finding of no likelihood of confusion, charging the appellate panel majority with misapplying the clear error standard of review and misconstruing several likelihood of confusion factors including strength of the mark, including the district court’s findings of conceptual and commercial weakness that Judge Engelhardt found to be supported by the trial record. Fifth Circuit Affirms Dismissal of IP Claims Due to Valid TTRPG Licensing Agreement – On Wednesday, November 4, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit issued a ruling in Thomas v. Leyline Publishing, L.L.C. affirming a summary judgment ruling by the Northern District of Texas dismissing a lawsuit including trademark and other intellectual property claims filed by tabletop role playing game (TTRPG) developer Shawn Thomas following a disagreement with game publisher Leyline over a licensing agreement to Thomas’ game “Realms of Kymoria.” The Fifth Circuit found that Leyline Publishing did not breach the licensing agreement for failure to pay for certain content before using it, including content for which Thomas had not yet billed Leyline, and that the district court correctly inferred a trademark license from the agreement’s language allowing Leyland to share the content it purchased under its own branding. AG Szpunar Tells CJEU That Google Gemini Chatbots May Infringe Press Rights – On Tuesday, November 3, Advocate General (AG) Maciej Szpunar of the Court of Justice for the European Union (CJEU) issued an opinion in the first generative artificial intelligence (AI) case to reach the CJEU, involving Google Gemini’s of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology to collect information in real-time from Internet sources to improve the reliability and accuracy of AI chatbot answers. Clarifying the circumstances under which such a process could infringe the rights of press publishers under EU law, AG Szpunar urged the CJEU to find that, as limited to answers provided by chatbots and not within the broader context of AI training, the reuse of content from a press publisher’s website may infringe those rights when the chatbot circumvents effective technical measures protecting the content, such as a paywall, or reuses any of the publication’s expression in a recognizable manner. Barks Copyright Office Extends Comment Period on Music Streaming Fraud NOI to December 18 – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Copyright Office announced that the agency was extending the deadline for the submission of public comments in response to its October notice of inquiry (NOI) on streaming music fraud, with initial comments due December 18 and reply comments due January 29, 2027. Copyright Office Hits Milestone of 25,000 Digitized Copyright Historical Record Books – On Thursday, November 5, the U.S. Copyright Office announced that a total of 25,238 bound copyright historical record books have been digitized for inclusion in the Copyright Historical Record Books Collection, which now contains more than 21.7 million images of copyright applications and other records bound in books dating from 1870 to 1977. Trademark Suit Filed in District of Minnesota Between “JOHNNIES” Collegiate Athletic Programs – On Thursday, November 4, the Collegeville, MN-based school Saint John’s University filed a lawsuit alleging claims of trademark infringement in the District of Minnesota against New York City-based St. John’s University alleging a likelihood of consumer confusion over the use of the “JOHNNIES” trademark, registered by Minnesota’s Saint John’s school and used by both universities to refer to teams within their respective athletic departments. Second Circuit Affirms Willful Counterfeiting Verdict, $4M Statutory Damages for Chanel – On Tuesday, November 3, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit issued a summary order in Chanel, Inc. v. What Goes Around Comes Around LLC affirming an award of $4 million in statutory damages to Chanel for What Goes Around’s use of a counterfeit mark over sales of stolen or otherwise missing Chanel merchandise removed from that company’s ORLI internal inventory system. Tenth Circuit Dismisses Copyright Damages Appeal for Lack of Appellate Jurisdiction – On Tuesday, November 3, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit issued a ruling in The Capture Eleven Group v. Otter Products, LLC dismissing cross-appeals from a jury verdict awarding Capture Eleven $3 million in profit disgorgement and $114,000 in actual damages for copyright infringement after finding the district court’s order granting a stipulated motion for certification under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b) as the order did not clearly articulate reasons and make careful statements regarding finality in light of third-party litigation in the case. Second Circuit Affirms Prison Sentence, Restitution in Criminal Counterfeiting Case – On Tuesday, November 3, the Second Circuit issued a ruling in United States v. Sow affirming the Southern District of New York’s judgment sentencing Adama Sow to 24 months’ imprisonment, three years’ supervised release and more than $111,000 in restitution after pleading guilty to one count of trafficking in counterfeit goods related to trafficking at least $3.1 million in counterfeit luxury goods through a Gotham Mini-Storage facility in Manhattan. This Week on Wall Street Massive Tech Stock Selloff on AI Regulatory Concerns Could Delay Anthropic IPO – On Thursday, November 5, international news agency Reuters reported on comments provided to Reuters from those familiar with discussions between potential investors and AI company Anthropic that this week’s massive tech stock selloff following this year’s midterm elections, leading to concerns in the data center business world over enhanced regulatory scrutiny by Democrats, which could delay Anthropic’s intention to launch an initial public offering (IPO) of company stock at the company’s current $1.5 trillion valuation. Provider News Provider News Seattle Children’s Providing Influenza and COVID-19 Vaccinations to Patients Nov. 4, 2026 As the annual viral surge continues to grow, it’s important to provide easy access for pediatric patients to receive influenza and COVID-19 vaccinations to reduce the spread of illness. Please review the information below about how current Seattle Children’s patients can access vaccinations. Vaccinations given to patients will be documented in the Child Profile Immunization Registry. For questions about influenza and COVID-19 vaccinations at Seattle Children’s, please visit seattlechildrens.org. Influenza Vaccines at Seattle Children’s Influenza vaccines are available to current patients at Seattle Children’s Hospital and subspecialty and regional clinics, including patients in its urgent care locations and the emergency department. Patients will be screened for eligibility. Seattle Children’s will also provide downloadable flu shot vouchers to patients’ family members and household contacts ages 3 years and older during patient visits; the vouchers can be used at any Albertsons-owned pharmacies and stores with no out-of-pocket cost (family members’ insurance will be billed if available, and any remaining balance will be charged to Seattle Children’s). Family members and household contacts from 6 months to 35 months old will need to get their flu vaccine at their primary care provider’s office. COVID-19 Vaccines at Seattle Children’s COVID-19 vaccines are available for patients ages 6 months and older who are currently admitted or on-site for a clinic appointment. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Sunday, November 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Twelve-Week Olfactory Training Improves Persistent Post-COVID-19 Smell Loss in Randomized Trial by November 6, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Twelve-Week Olfactory Training Improves Persistent Post-COVID-19 Smell Loss in Randomized Trial Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A twelve-week regimen of structured olfactory training led to significant and clinically meaningful improvements in smell function among adults experiencing persistent olfactory dysfunction after SARS-CoV-2 infection, according to results from a single-centre, randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded trial. The study, designated as the SMELL trial, addressed a condition that is common, prolonged, and disabling following infection, and for which validated therapeutic options have remained limited. Investigators evaluated adult participants aged 18 years and older who had experienced at least three months of ongoing olfactory dysfunction after a documented SARS-CoV-2 infection and who demonstrated measurable baseline impairment on Sniffin’ Sticks identification testing. Because the trial protocol was designed during the COVID-19 pandemic under contemporaneous infection-control recommendations, the researchers implemented specific methodological modifications to ensure participant safety. Olfactory assessments were performed by drawing an odor line onto single-use filter paper strips rather than presenting the reusable Sniffin’ Stick pen directly beneath each participant’s nose. This technique proved feasible for conducting both Sniffin’ Stick identification and Sniffin’ Stick discrimination testing; however, it was not feasible for odor threshold assessment, which was consequently omitted. To account for this adaptation, the study used a prespecified modified Sniffin’ Sticks total score, calculated by combining the identification and discrimination scores, with the primary study endpoint defined as the change in this modified total score from baseline to twelve weeks. Study screening proceeded through October 31, 2024, during which a total of 77 candidates were assessed. From this screened group, 70 participants were randomly assigned either to undergo twelve weeks of olfactory training or to receive no intervention, representing the natural course of recovery. A total of 68 participants completed the randomized phase of the trial and were included in the primary per-protocol analysis, consisting of 38 participants allocated to the active olfactory training intervention and 30 participants allocated to the untreated control group. Discover more Find ENT Doctors Read Med Journals Study Anatomy COVID-19 Get Rapid Tests The trial demonstrated that twelve weeks of olfactory training significantly improved modified Sniffin’ Sticks total scores compared with the control condition, yielding a statistically significant time-by-group interaction of F(1, 66) = 29.95 (p < 0.001; partial η2 = 0.31). Statistically significant interaction effects favouring the intervention were likewise observed across both subcomponents, with identification scores achieving p < 0.001 (partial η2 = 0.27) and discrimination scores achieving p < 0.001 (partial η2 = 0.19). Protocol-defined clinically relevant improvement in the modified total score occurred in 22 of 38 participants (57.9%) in the olfactory training arm compared to 2 of 30 participants (6.7%) in the control group (φ = 0.53, p < 0.001). Furthermore, assessments of global improvement reported by patients and evaluated by clinicians independently favoured the olfactory training group. Predefined subgroup evaluations confirmed consistent treatment benefits among individuals whose olfactory loss had persisted for more than 6 months as well as those with ongoing loss exceeding 12 months. In addition, participants initially assigned to the control group who subsequently received training during an exploratory extension phase demonstrated significant gains in total modified scores, identification scores, and discrimination scores. No serious adverse events occurred throughout the trial, leading the study team to conclude that structured olfactory training offers a safe, practical, and scalable treatment option for persistent post-COVID-19 smell dysfunction. records.content: Canada becomes the first country to authorize both Moderna’s mRNA seasonal influenza vaccine, mFLUSIVA ® , and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine, mCOFLU ® CAMBRIDGE, MA / ACCESS Newswire / November 5, 2026 / Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today announced that Health Canada has authorized mFLUSIVA ® (Influenza mRNA vaccine; mRNA-1010) and mCOFLU ® (Combined Influenza and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine; mRNA-1083) for adults 50 years of age and older. Canada is the first country in the world to authorize both Moderna’s seasonal mRNA influenza vaccine and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine. “Health Canada’s authorizations of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU today mark another important step in bringing the benefits of mRNA technology to seasonal respiratory vaccination. It’s not every day that a company gets two product approvals on the same day,” said Stéphane Bancel, Chief Executive Officer of Moderna. “Influenza and COVID-19 continue to place a significant burden on public health, particularly among older adults. These milestones reflect our commitment to advancing innovative vaccine options that help protect Canadians and support more resilient health systems.” mFLUSIVA is Canada’s first mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, while mCOFLU is the country’s first combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine. Health Canada’s authorizations follow the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s approval of mFLUSIVA in August 2026 and the European Commission’s authorization of the Company’s combination influenza and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, marketed as mCOMBRIAX®, in April 2026. Both vaccines remain under regulatory review in additional markets. mFLUSIVA is authorized for active immunization of adults 50 years of age and older for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus subtypes A and B represented in the vaccine. i mCOFLU is authorized for active immunization of adults 50 years of age and older for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus types A and B represented in the vaccine and SARS-CoV-2. ii Health Canada’s authorization of mFLUSIVA is supported by the pivotal Phase 3 mRNA-1010-P304 study (NCT06602024), a randomized, active-controlled trial involving approximately 40,800 adults 50 years of age and older across 11 countries. mFLUSIVA met all pre-specified statistical success criteria, including the highest level of pre-specified superiority, demonstrating relative vaccine efficacy of 26.6% (95% CI: 16.7-35.4) in adults 50 years of age and older and 27.4% (95% CI: 12.1-40.0) in adults 65 years of age and older compared with a standard-dose inactivated influenza vaccine against RT-PCR-confirmed, protocol-defined influenza-like illness caused by influenza A or B. iii The authorization is also supported by the Phase 3 mRNA-1010-P303 Part C study (NCT05827978), which demonstrated superior antibody responses compared with a high-dose inactivated influenza vaccine in adults 65 years of age and older. iv Across both studies, the most commonly reported adverse reactions included injection-site pain, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, chills and axillary (underarm) swelling or tenderness. Most solicited reactions were mild to moderate and resolved within one to two days. v mCOFLU builds on the clinical development of mFLUSIVA and mNEXSPIKE ® . Health Canada’s authorization of mCOFLU is supported by a pivotal Phase 3 trial (NCT06097273), a randomized, observer-blind, active-controlled study evaluating safety, reactogenicity and immunogenicity in two cohorts of approximately 4,000 adults each. Adults 65 years of age and older received mCOFLU or co-administered Fluzone HD ® , a high-dose influenza vaccine, and Spikevax ® , Moderna’s licensed COVID-19 vaccine. Adults 50 to 64 years of age received mCOFLU or co-administered Fluarix ® , a standard-dose influenza vaccine, and Spikevax. vi The study met all primary endpoints demonstrating non-inferiority of immune responses. Following a single dose, mCOFLU elicited statistically significantly higher immune responses against three influenza strains (A/H1N1, A/H3N2 and B/Victoria) and SARS-CoV-2 in both age cohorts compared with co-administered licensed comparator vaccines. The exception was B/Yamagata, a strain no longer recommended for inclusion in seasonal influenza vaccines, for which a statistically significantly higher immune response was not observed in adults 65 years of age and older. vii mCOFLU demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile. The most commonly reported adverse reactions included injection-site pain, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, joint pain, chills and axillary (underarm) swelling or tenderness. Most were mild to moderate and short in duration. No serious adverse events were assessed as related to mCOFLU in the pivotal study. viii Moderna will engage with Canadian health authorities and immunization partners as it advances plans for the future availability of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU in Canada. About Moderna Moderna is a pioneer and leader in the field of mRNA medicine. Through the advancement of its technology platform, Moderna is reimagining how medicines are made to transform how we treat and prevent diseases. Since its founding, Moderna’s mRNA platform has enabled the development of vaccines and therapeutics across infectious diseases, cancer, rare diseases and more. With a global team and a unique culture, driven by the company’s values and mindsets, Moderna’s mission is to deliver the greatest possible impact to people through mRNA medicines. For more information about Moderna, please visit modernatx.com and connect with us on X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and LinkedIn. mFLUSIVA ® , mCOFLU ® , Spikevax ® , mCOMBRIAX ® and mNEXSPIKE ® are registered trademarks of Moderna. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended, including regarding: Moderna’s engagement with Canadian health authorities and immunization partners; the future availability of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU in Canada; the potential of Moderna’s mRNA platform to advance respiratory disease prevention; and the review of additional regulatory applications of Moderna’s influenza and combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccines in other markets. The forward-looking statements in this press release are neither promises nor guarantees, and you should not place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements because they involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors, many of which are beyond Moderna’s control and which could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by these forward-looking statements. These risks, uncertainties, and other factors include those other risks and uncertainties described under the heading “Risk Factors” in Moderna’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and in subsequent filings made by Moderna with the SEC, which are available on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov . Except as required by law, Moderna disclaims any intention or responsibility for updating or revising any forward-looking statements contained in this press release in the event of new information, future developments or otherwise. These forward-looking statements are based on Moderna’s current expectations and speak only as of the date hereof. See also Leroux-Roels I, Huang G, Ferguson M, et al. “Efficacy and Safety of an mRNA Seasonal Influenza Vaccine in Adults.” New England Journal of Medicine . 2026;394(18):1803-1813. iv Moderna Biopharma Canada Corp. mFLUSIVA® Product Monograph , November 4, 2026, Section 14 (Clinical Trials), including Study mRNA-1010-P303 Part C immunogenicity and safety data. v Moderna Biopharma Canada Corp. mFLUSIVA® Product Monograph , November 4, 2026, Section 8 (Adverse Reactions). vi Moderna Biopharma Canada Corp. mCOFLU® Product Monograph , November 4, 2026, Control No. 303836, Section 14 (Clinical Trials). vii Moderna Biopharma Canada Corp. mCOFLU® Product Monograph , November 4, 2026, Control No. 303836, Section 14 (Clinical Trials). viii Moderna Biopharma Canada Corp. mCOFLU® Product Monograph , November 4, 2026, Control No. 303836, Section 8 (Adverse Reactions), including Study mRNA-1083-P301 (NCT06097273). A ‘Draw, Write and Tell’ Exploration of Children's Postpandemic Understanding of COVID-19 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月08日 来源:Child: Care, Health and Development 2 编辑推荐: 目的:本研究旨在采用“绘画-书写-讲述”(Draw, Write and Tell, DWT)方法探索后疫情时代儿童对COVID-19的认知。研究基于常识模型(Common Sense Model, CSM)的特征评估儿童绘画的准确性,考察其发展趋势,并探索儿 欢迎领取“抗体偶联药物前沿研发方案” 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 RESEARCH ARTICLE Open Access 目的:本研究旨在采用“绘画-书写-讲述”(Draw, Write and Tell, DWT)方法探索后疫情时代儿童对COVID-19的认知。研究基于常识模型(Common Sense Model, CSM)的特征评估儿童绘画的准确性,考察其发展趋势,并探索儿童在绘画中赋予COVID-19的视觉表征。设计:采用横断面参与式设计,在个体数据收集环节中运用DWT方法。方法:70名5–11岁儿童通过绘画和文字创作描绘COVID-19的图画,随后向研究人员描述其作品。数据在学校中个别收集。完整的视觉制品由儿童原始绘画、附带文字及研究人员标注组成。采用内容分析与反思性主题分析的双重方法对制品进行分析。结果:年长儿童对COVID-19的表征显著更为准确。准确性在CSM衍生的身份(Identity)、严重性(Severity)和病因(Cause)维度上最高,而对时间线(Timeline)、可治愈性(Curability)和治疗(Treatment)的理解在所有年龄组中均持续偏低。围绕儿童对COVID-19的认知构建了两个主题:COVID-19作为一种疾病和COVID-19作为一种生物实体。值得注意的是,所有年龄段的儿童均将COVID-19拟人化,年长儿童更倾向于如此。最后,儿童讨论了其COVID-19信息来源。结论:儿童对COVID-19的认知具有多面性,既涵盖疾病概念,也包括其生物学病因。这在后疫情时代对于设计和传播适合儿童发展阶段的健康信息宣传活动及小学阶段的生物学教育具有更广泛的启示。 **研究背景与问题** 欢迎领取《抗体药研发解决方案》领 取 自2020年疫情暴发以来,COVID-19作为一种隐性且复杂的威胁,深刻扰乱了日常生活的各个方面。由于这场前所未有的公共卫生紧急事件,健康信息宣传活动无处不在,但这些信息主要由成人设计并面向成人传播(Bray, Blake, et al. 2021; Christidou et al. 2021; Rowland and Cook 2021; Thompson et al. 2021)。儿童因此成为关于SARS-CoV-2及其传播风险和预防措施信息的间接接收者。一项大规模报告(G?tz et al. 2020)指出了这一差异的影响,结论认为儿童在掌握部分COVID-19知识的同时感到担忧,并能从更适合其年龄的信息中受益。自2023年5月起(World Health Organisation [WHO] 2023),COVID-19不再构成国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(Public Health Emergency of International Concern, PHEIC)。然而,这一背景为理解儿童如何概念化新发传染病提供了独特情境。探索儿童对COVID-19的视觉表征,作为使其隐性概念化变得可见的途径,可为未来面向儿童的健康信息传播提供关键框架。以往关于儿童健康威胁认知的发展趋势因疾病类型而异。儿童对AIDS的理解比流感更为详细,这归因于AIDS流行期间的信息暴露(Sigelman 2022)。其他疾病如水痘或麻疹相对被较好理解,各年龄段儿童均表现出对预防和康复的知识(Bir and Podmore 1990)。探索儿童对COVID-19认知的文献较为稀少。Thompson et al.(2021)发现儿童对COVID-19的理解涵盖三个主题:COVID-19作为一种传染性疾病、围绕疫情的负面情绪和社会责任。后者为疾病构念提供了一个有趣的组成部分,因为它在其他疾病的认知中并未出现。Labotka and Gelman(2023)报告称儿童对COVID-19和普通感冒的理解基本相似;然而当存在差异时,儿童对COVID-19的概念化准确性高于普通感冒。关键在于,上述数据均收集于疫情期间,当时关于COVID-19的信息无处不在。疫情之后儿童对COVID-19认知的这种高准确性是否得以保持,仍属未知。本研究采用Leventhal et al.(1980, 1992, 2016)的常识模型(CSM)作为组织儿童疾病感知细微差异的适当框架,该模型由五个核心维度组成:身份(Identity)、病因(Cause)、时间线(Timeline)、后果(Consequences)和控制(Control)。尽管该框架最初针对成人设计,但已有效用于组织儿童对不同疾病状况和以往流行病(如流感、普通感冒、AIDS和H1N1流感)的表征(e.g., Karademas et al. 2013; Law et al. 2014; Myant and Williams 2005; Williams et al. 2012; Wong and Sam 2011)。在CSM框架内已观察到发展趋势,年长儿童在病因、时间线、可治愈性和后果维度上表现出更好的理解(Fox et al. 2008; Wickering et al. 2023)。将CSM作为COVID-19研究框架的工作相对较少(e.g., Hayes et al. 2022; M?ller et al. 2022),且尚未有研究将CSM应用于儿童对COVID-19的认知。绘画此前已被用作阐明儿童和成人CSM维度的有效工具(Broadbent et al. 2019)。“绘画-书写-讲述”(DWT)是一种多功能的创造性研究方法,要求参与者根据提示提供绘画、包含标注并向研究人员描述其创作(Angell et al. 2015)。长期以来,它被认为是探索儿童健康和疾病认知的有用工具(e.g., Bradding and Horstman 1999; Liamputtong and Fernandes 2015; Pope et al. 2019; Xie et al. 2022),且不依赖复杂的语言技能(McWhirter 2014)。尽管儿童绘画能够有效探索其对COVID-19的认知(e.g., Bonoti et al. 2022; Christidou et al. 2021),但DWT尚未应用于此背景。年幼儿童在绘制微生物时倾向于使用拟人化,这一趋势随年龄增长和对生物学理解的深化而减弱(Byrne 2011)。有趣的是,Labotka and Gelman(2023)在探索儿童对COVID-19的认知时发现这一趋势发生了逆转,年长儿童比年幼儿童更多地将微生物拟人化。因此,DWT方法在深入捕捉儿童对COVID-19的认知方面具有独特优势。本研究是一个更大的多方法项目的一部分,该项目包括访谈和创造性方法,旨在考察儿童对COVID-19认知的发展变化。本文呈现的研究采用DWT方法探索后疫情时代儿童对COVID-19的认知,旨在:(1)基于CSM维度评估儿童绘画中所表征知识的准确性;(2)考察数据中的发展趋势;(3)探索儿童在绘画中赋予COVID-19的视觉表征:疾病、公共卫生信息和微生物。 **关键技术方法** 本研究采用横断面参与式设计,运用DWT方法进行个体数据收集。样本为70名5–11岁儿童(M = 8.5, SD = 2.1),均就读于英国苏格兰同一所国家资助小学,该区域属于苏格兰最不贫困的20%地区。数据收集于2023年11月至12月间共15天内在学校正常上课时间进行。每名儿童单独参与,被要求“你想让我看看COVID-19长什么样吗?你可以用绘画和文字”。完整的视觉制品包括儿童原始绘画、附带文字及研究人员标注。分析采用内容分析(基于CSM的九维度编码方案,评分0–3)和反思性主题分析的双重方法。定量数据使用R进行分析,采用非参数Wilcoxon秩和检验比较年幼组(5–7岁)和年长组(8–11岁)的准确性差异。 **研究结果** **内容分析**:年长儿童在CSM框架内对COVID-19的总体准确性中位数(0.44)显著高于年幼儿童(0.11)(W = 202.5, p < 0.001)。个体维度分析显示,身份(W = 360, p < 0.05)、严重性(W = 462, p < 0.05)和病因(W = 235, p < 0.001)维度的准确性在年长儿童中显著更高。然而,症状、预防、症状出现时间线、可治愈性、治疗和康复时间线在各年龄段均持续偏低,无显著变化。 **反思性主题分析**:构建了两个主题。主题1——COVID-19作为一种疾病,包含四个子主题:(1)感染COVID-19:涵盖传播机制和预防方法,儿童描绘了唾液、鼻、眼、手和污物等传播机制以及洗手、戴口罩和咳嗽时掩口等预防策略,但未将疫苗接种作为预防策略加以描绘;(2)患有COVID-19:涵盖生理、心理和社会方面,包括症状描述、情绪表达(最常见为悲伤,其次为愤怒和孤独)以及自我隔离或他人照护等社会层面;(3)COVID-19干预措施:包括状况评估(体温计、快速侧流抗原检测、PCR检测)和治疗(通用药物、居家 remedies、卧床休息),年长儿童更多提及状况评估而年幼儿童主要提及治疗;(4)COVID-19结局:呈现完全康复或死亡的二元结局,儿童多用文字描述而非绘画细节。主题2——COVID-19作为一种生物实体,包含六个子主题:(1)拟人化微生物:儿童赋予微生物人类特征、情感、社会动态和道德属性,年长儿童更倾向于描绘不道德行为;(2)微生物颜色:儿童使用颜色作为信息标记而非情感表达,最常见色调为绿色、红色和灰色,色相和饱和度均承载信息;(3)刺突功能:儿童对刺突功能提供了精细解释,包括维持结构完整性、防御其他细胞、感染机制、导航、移动和吸附等,该子主题平均年龄最高(11岁);(4)感染过程:儿童将感染过程呈现为病毒在体内增殖或接管健康细胞,并提及免疫系统的作用;(5)微生物数量:儿童绘制单个或多个微生物,绘制单个微生物的儿童年龄略大;(6)信息来源:儿童主要引用图像和视频作为信息来源,年长儿童更多引用视频,无儿童提及父母或教师作为直接信息来源。 **讨论与结论** 本研究采用DWT方法探索后疫情时代小学生对COVID-19的认知。通过内容分析和反思性主题分析的双重方法,揭示了儿童COVID-19概念的多面性和复杂性。内容分析作为演绎方法,表明儿童对COVID-19的认知存在明显的发展进程,年长儿童总体准确性更高,尤其在身份、严重性和病因维度;而时间线、可治愈性和治疗维度在各年龄段均持续偏低,这种不对称性提示某些方面可能更具发展敏感性,凸显了教育干预的重点领域。反思性主题分析作为归纳方法,深化了对儿童视觉表征的洞察。COVID-19被描绘为兼具生物学、心理学和社会表征的复杂概念。儿童对病毒刺突功能的归因是此前文献未讨论的独特发现,揭示了儿童构建科学意义的方式,表明其存在朴素生物学(na?ve biology)(Hatano and Inagaki 1994)。与传统的Piagetian视角不同,所有年龄段儿童均将COVID-19拟人化,年长儿童更倾向如此,这与Labotka and Gelman(2023)的发现一致。拟人化以不同方式出现,包括感知性拟人化,支持Airenti(2018)关于拟人化是基本人类态度而非儿童特有的论点。儿童还赋予病毒情感状态和道德倾向,这可能归因于英国公共卫生信息中的道德基调以及效果性动机(effectance motivation)以创造控制感(Waytz et al. 2010)。疾病相关情绪有所呈现,但明显缺乏恐惧和积极情绪,这可能归因于疫情已过去的时间。儿童未提及父母或教师作为信息来源,而是提及新闻或图像,这与Bray, Carter, et al.(2021)疫情期间国际研究形成鲜明对比,提示儿童健康信息获取在后疫情时代可能发生了转变。研究结论:本研究表明白小学生将COVID-19理解为多面性概念。儿童绘画中识别出明确的发展趋势,年长儿童在CSM的身份、严重性和病因维度上概念化准确性更高。无论年龄,时间线和可治愈性维度均存在知识差距,表明CSM各维度被不均衡地理解。此外,儿童绘画清晰展现了其对COVID-19的认知超越CSM维度,COVID-19既涵盖疾病概念也包括其生物实体,涉及拟人化、道德、朴素生物学和社会责任。这些结果在后疫情时代对设计和传播适合儿童发展阶段的健康信息宣传活动及小学阶段生物学教育具有更广泛的启示。
