records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Sunday, November 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Machine Learning and Topological Analysis Identify COVID-19 in Lung Scans by November 8, 2026 in Health, Technology Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Machine Learning and Topological Analysis Identify COVID-19 in Lung Scans Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A mathematical imaging framework combining topological data analysis with supervised machine learning algorithms has achieved an accuracy rate of 97.5 percent and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve exceeding 0.99 in detecting COVID-19 from axial chest computed tomography scans. In an experimental evaluation reported by researchers Rabih Assaf, Abbas Rammal, Alban Goupil, Mohammad Kacim, and Valeriu Vrabie, persistent homology was applied to extract multi-scale structural descriptors of lung parenchyma, which were subsequently supplied to various automated classification architectures. The resulting experimental outcomes established that a Random Forest classifier attained a peak classification accuracy of 97.51 percent at a thirty percent testing split, while a Support Vector Machine utilizing a radial basis function kernel achieved the highest overall area under the curve value of 0.992495. By systematically capturing intrinsic geometric and homological structures within chest scans rather than depending exclusively on raw pixel intensity matrices or traditional localized pixel statistics, this analytical configuration demonstrates an automated diagnostic methodology capable of identifying viral pulmonary alterations across complex radiological datasets. The clinical motivation outlined in the investigation centers on the persistent vulnerabilities of established pathogenic diagnostic procedures alongside the operational challenges posed by global viral dissemination. While pathogenic laboratory examinations such as reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction testing remain the prevailing diagnostic standard for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, they carry notable operational limitations including processing turnaround delays and documented frequencies of false-negative outcomes. Conventional molecular tests identify viral genetic sequences directly from respiratory specimens, whereas rapid antigen screenings identify viral surface proteins at lower sensitivity, and serological examinations identify host antibody production but cannot diagnose acute phase illnesses. Consequently, chest radiography and computed tomography imaging modalities serve as vital adjunctive diagnostic pathways capable of highlighting pulmonary damage patterns, including ground-glass opacities, lung consolidations, and fine reticular anomalies that perturb the anatomical architecture of healthy lung tissue. To resolve these radiological challenges rapidly without overwhelming clinical facilities, the researchers formulated an automated computational pipeline designed to process high-dimensional radiological data, discern infection-induced structural alterations, and provide consistent classification without relying on subjective human observation. To capture high-dimensional geometric arrangements that evade classical statistical distributions, the proposed technique introduces concepts grounded in algebraic topology through topological data analysis. Unlike traditional geometrical models that simplify shapes into rudimentary cell complexes and lose fine quantitative information, topological data analysis extracts coarse-scale, global, and nonlinear structural invariants from spatial datasets. In this radiological implementation, two-dimensional grayscale lung slice images are formally converted into topological cubical complexes, designated as pixels complexes, wherein individual image pixels function as zero-dimensional vertices or zero-cells. Spatial connections between horizontally or vertically adjacent pixels differing by a single spatial unit coordinate are mapped as unit-length edges or one-cells, and the bounded regions enclosed by four perimeter edges are defined as unit squares or two-cells. This formal construction yields an integrated algebraic structure that simultaneously encapsulates discrete numerical pixel intensities alongside their exact spatial neighborhoods, generating a rigorous geometric baseline from which multi-scale topological features can be consistently measured across diverse radiological densities. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Biotech startup funding Within the algebraic structure of the constructed pixels complex, formal linear combinations of k-cells are organized into k-chains with coefficients belonging to the binary finite field of integers modulo two. The aggregate set of these k-chains constitutes a sequence of chain groups interconnected by boundary operators that map k-dimensional chains directly into boundary chains of dimension k minus one. The mathematical integrity of this system relies on the fundamental topological condition establishing that the composition of successive boundary operators yields zero for every dimension, meaning that the boundary of a boundary is identically empty. Elements whose boundaries evaluate to zero constitute the k-th cycle subgroup, representing closed loops or voids that encircle spatial cavities without enclosing solid matter. Concurrently, elements formed by taking the boundary of higher-dimensional chains constitute the k-th boundary subgroup. Because the boundary subgroup forms a proper subset of the cycle subgroup, algebraic quotient groups designated as homology groups are formed by factoring cycle groups by their boundary groups. These quotient groups isolate persistent structural cavities, such as zero-dimensional connected components and one-dimensional enclosing loops, while mathematically discarding trivial boundaries. Because single static evaluations of homology groups fail to capture the evolutionary trajectory of spatial features across brightness gradients, the researchers instituted an intensity-driven filtration scheme to compute persistent homology. Under this ordering protocol, zero-cells inherit values directly corresponding to image pixel intensities, whereas each higher-dimensional k-cell is systematically assigned the maximum intensity exhibited among the lower-dimensional cells forming its immediate boundary. As a numerical threshold parameter advances monotonically, a nested sequence of expanding subcomplexes emerges, spanning from the empty set through the entire image complex. Throughout this sequential expansion, topological cavities emerge at specific birth thresholds and eventually terminate or merge into higher-dimensional structures at subsequent death thresholds. The lifespan of any topological class is computed as the quantitative difference between its destruction level and creation level, with prolonged lifespans designating stable, prominent structural properties of pulmonary tissue and brief lifespans representing radiological image noise. These multidimensional birth and death coordinates are summarized through persistence diagrams and persistence barcodes, calculated programmatically utilizing the Persistent Homology Algorithm Toolbox. From the persistent homology computations and standard image properties, the investigators engineered a compact vector comprising eight numerical features extracted from each processed lung computed tomography image. These eight quantitative descriptors encompass the mean lifespan and standard deviation of zero-dimensional homology cycles, the mean lifespan and standard deviation of one-dimensional homology cycles, the zero-dimensional persistent entropy, the one-dimensional persistent entropy, alongside the overall mean and standard deviation of image pixel intensities. Persistent entropy quantifies the structural diversity of the topological landscape by evaluating the normalized ratio of individual cycle lifespans against the aggregate sum of all lifespans through a logarithmic entropy formulation. These computed descriptors were then provided to five supervised machine learning models: Decision Trees as a logic-based classifier requiring no prior distributional assumptions, Random Forest as an ensemble tree model, Support Vector Machines utilizing a radial basis function kernel, Gaussian Naive Bayes reflecting conditional predictor probabilities, and Logistic Regression representing linear statistical modeling. The experimental dataset comprised eight hundred axial chest computed tomography scans collected in equal balance, consisting of four hundred images from confirmed COVID-19 patients and four hundred scans from healthy individuals without viral abnormalities. To eliminate radiological confounders and extraneous non-pulmonary anatomical structures, the team deployed an image preprocessing sequence beginning with spatial resizing that standardized all heterogeneous scans to dimensions of 128 by 128 pixels. The images were subsequently converted to a 256-level grayscale colormap and normalized to floating-point numerical values within a zero-to-one range. To amplify radiological contrast between the lung parenchyma and surrounding thoracic elements such as ribs, soft tissues, blood vessels, and cardiac structures, gamma correction contrast enhancement was implemented using a gamma parameter value of three, notably omitting artificial noise-reduction filters. Lung segmentation was subsequently performed by executing binary and triangle thresholding for normal scans alongside Otsu thresholding for COVID-19 scans, followed by mask generation to eliminate out-lung artifacts while retaining purely pulmonary parenchymal regions. Model training and evaluation were carried out using varying train-test dataset splits alongside k-fold cross-validation frameworks to verify predictive stability across unseen samples. The cross-validation protocol partitioned the processed imagery across multiple fold configurations including three, four, five, and ten folds, iteratively utilizing each partitioned subset for validation while remaining subsets served for model fitting. In baseline single-split evaluations, the Decision Tree classifier recorded an overall accuracy of 93.75 percent, an F1 score of 0.94, and an area under the curve of 0.93812 at a twenty percent testing split, demonstrating mean cross-validation accuracy of 91.72 percent with a standard deviation of 1.31 percent. The Logistic Regression model achieved a peak accuracy of 85.42 percent at a thirty percent testing split with an average area under the curve of 0.945505 and a cross-validation mean accuracy of 83.86 percent with a standard deviation of 1.03 percent. The Naive Bayes classifier demonstrated lower relative efficacy, recording an average accuracy of 84.09 percent, an F1 score of 0.8559, an area under the curve of 0.948845, and a cross-validation mean accuracy of 84.11 percent with a standard deviation of 1.64 percent across fold evaluations. The Random Forest and Support Vector Machine models demonstrated the highest performance across all quantitative evaluation metrics. The Random Forest classifier attained an accuracy of 97.51 percent at a thirty percent testing split, sustaining an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve above 0.99 across all testing sizes, alongside a cross-validation accuracy mean of 96.34 percent and a standard deviation of 0.72 percent across folds. The Support Vector Machine recorded a peak accuracy of 96.25 percent at a thirty percent testing split and established the highest area under the curve value among all models at 0.992495, maintaining a cross-validation accuracy mean of 94.51 percent with a standard deviation of 0.95 percent. The investigators noted that the Random Forest architecture derived stability from averaging decision trees to curtail prediction variance, while the Support Vector Machine benefited from mapping the linear algebraic formulations of homological features into higher-dimensional kernel space, distinctly separating pathological patterns from normal parenchymal variations. To rigorously verify the diagnostic necessity of the topological features, the authors executed ablation trials comparing performance when removing either topological or statistical descriptors from the models. When the identical classifiers were trained using solely the two basic pixel statistics of mean and standard deviation, maximum accuracy dropped to 94.7 percent and area under the curve reached 0.97328. Conversely, training on the six persistent homology features alone without pixel statistics yielded a maximum accuracy of 85.4 percent and an area under the curve of 0.86519, confirming that combining homological descriptors with statistical metrics achieves optimal predictive capability. External validation on a separate independent computed tomography dataset corroborated this performance, with the Support Vector Machine reaching 94.5 percent accuracy with an area under the curve of 0.93 and the Random Forest reaching 93.8 percent accuracy with an area under the curve of 0.94. Benchmarking against convolutional neural networks with three and four layers coupled to the classifiers demonstrated comparable peak accuracies between 92.3 and 95.7 percent, while remaining computationally distinct. The authors explicitly emphasize several operational limitations, noting that clinical variability in image quality, scanner equipment, motion artifacts, and low slice resolution could degrade classification performance in actual medical deployments, while persistent homology values lack the intuitive visual interpretability of traditional clinical biomarkers, necessitating expanded validation across diverse thoracic imaging formats and patient prognostic trajectories before clinical implementation. (2025). Topological data analysis and machine learning for COVID-19 detection in CT scan lung images. The study, conducted by researchers Anbarasan K. and C. Sasikala, applied a standardized in silico docking protocol to compare how alkaloid, flavonoid, polyphenol, sterol, and triterpenoid scaffolds interact with the enzyme known as 3CLpro or Mpro. Across the tested panel, predicted binding free energies ranged from −6.43 kcal/mol to −11.43 kcal/mol, with the glycosylated flavonoid Rutin and the sterols Stigmasterol and β-Sitosterol exhibiting the most favorable predicted computational affinity scores. The target of the investigation, the SARS-CoV-2 main protease, is an essential viral enzyme responsible for cleaving large polyproteins into functional non-structural proteins required for viral replication and transcription machinery, including enzymes for RNA synthesis. Because the main protease is indispensable for viral maturation and features a conserved catalytic center based on the His41 and Cys145 dyad, it represents a primary focal point for antiviral inhibitor discovery. Additionally, scientific literature notes that the protease modulates host-cell pathways linked to innate immune defence and programmed cell death, and its activity has been suggested to play a role in systemic inflammatory manifestations observed during severe infection. Consequently, identifying small molecules capable of obstructing its active site remains an active avenue in antiviral development. Natural products and traditional healthcare systems, including India’s Siddha medicine, provide extensive reservoirs of structurally diverse secondary metabolites. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Siddha-based interventions gained public and clinical attention, particularly in Tamil Nadu where select traditional treatments were introduced into designated care facilities. Among these preparations is Sivanethirachooranam, a formulation classified under Gunapadam Mooligai that utilizes the seed of Elaeocarpus sphaericus, locally known as Rudraksha, which is purified, finely powdered, and traditionally combined with honey to manage conditions categorized in Siddha practice as sannipatha thodam, vikkal, pitta-associated dizziness, and specific kapha-related disorders. However, because clinical validation for many traditional botanical formulations is frequently constrained by heterogeneous trial designs and small cohorts, computational molecular modeling provides a preliminary screening method to assess whether individual constituents exhibit direct mechanistic affinity for viral targets. Discover more Study Chemistry chemical constituents Identify Plants Study Biology Get Rapid Tests To establish a controlled comparative framework, the researchers selected nine phytochemicals representing two plant sources: Elaeocarpus sphaericus and Aristolochia indica. Four compounds—Elaeocarpine, Grandisines, Quercetin, and Ellagic acid—were derived from reported phytochemical literature on E. sphaericus, providing alkaloidal and polyphenolic frameworks. The remaining five compounds—β-Sitosterol, Stigmasterol, Friedelin, Cycloeucalenol, and Rutin—were selected based on the documented chemical constituents of A. indica, supplying sterol, triterpenoid, and complex flavonoid glycoside scaffolds. Because earlier literature had already documented individual computational assessments for several of these molecules, the explicit purpose of this investigation was not to assert first-time discovery of binding activity, but to systematically analyze how scaffold rigidity, molecular weight, hydrogen-bonding capacity, and hydrophobic surface area alter binding geometry under identical AutoDock conditions. Before docking simulations commenced, two-dimensional structures were built using ChemDraw Professional version 12.0 and converted to three-dimensional conformations, followed by geometry optimization and energy minimization via the Merck Molecular Force Field 94 to eliminate unfavorable steric strain. Physicochemical characterization revealed notable structural variation across the ligand set, with molecular weights spanning from 257.33 g/mol for Elaeocarpine to 610.5 g/mol for Rutin. Grandisines, Quercetin, and Ellagic acid exhibited intermediate molecular masses of 276.37 g/mol, 302.23 g/mol, and 302.194 g/mol, respectively. In contrast, the sterol and triterpenoid derivatives displayed higher molecular weights, with Stigmasterol at 412.7 g/mol, β-Sitosterol at 414.7 g/mol, and both Friedelin and Cycloeucalenol at 426.7 g/mol. Conformational flexibility also diverged sharply: Elaeocarpine, Grandisines, Ellagic acid, and Friedelin presented zero rotatable bonds, reflecting rigid structures, whereas Stigmasterol and Cycloeucalenol possessed five rotatable bonds, and β-Sitosterol and Rutin each contained six. Discover more Find Lung Care Read Med Journals Check Symptoms The structural model chosen for the viral target was the experimentally determined crystal structure of SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro complexed with inhibitor N3, retrieved from the RCSB Protein Data Bank under accession code PDB ID: 6LU7, solved at an X-ray crystallographic resolution of 2.16 Å with an R value of approximately 0.202. Using AutoDock Tools, water molecules and the co-crystallized N3 ligand were stripped, polar hydrogen atoms were added, Kollman united-atom charges were applied, and solvation parameters were established. Validation through the MolProbity server confirmed high stereochemical quality, placing 97.05% of protein residues within favored regions of the Ramachandran plot with zero residues in disallowed regions, alongside an overall Ramachandran Z-score of −1.92 ± 0.41 and 87.17% of side-chain rotamers residing in favored conformations. The docking grid was constructed with AutoGrid, centered at coordinates x = −9.732 Å, y = 11.403 Å, and z = 68.925 Å with a 60 × 60 × 60 point grid box and 0.375 Å spacing, encompassing His41, Cys145, and the broader substrate-binding cleft. Simulations utilized the Lamarckian Genetic Algorithm coupled with Solis and Wets local searching across two independent runs per compound, capping energy evaluations at 250,000 per run with an initial population of 150 individuals, a translational step size of 0.2 Å, and rotational and torsional step sizes of 5°. When the resulting poses were ranked by calculated binding free energy, Rutin demonstrated the strongest predicted binding affinity at −11.43 kcal/mol, paired with a calculated inhibition constant of 4.19 nM, an electrostatic energy contribution of −0.03 kcal/mol, an intermolecular energy of −6.73 kcal/mol, and a total interaction surface of 840.57 Å2. In comparison, Stigmasterol achieved −9.66 kcal/mol with a calculated Ki of 82.60 mM, an intermolecular energy of −10.11 kcal/mol, and an interaction surface of 811.29 Å2, while β-Sitosterol scored −9.09 kcal/mol with a predicted Ki of 216.19 nM, an intermolecular energy of −10.37 kcal/mol, and the largest interaction surface area among all ligands at 946.79 Å2. The triterpenoids Friedelin and Cycloeucalenol produced docking free energies of −8.72 kcal/mol and −8.68 kcal/mol, accompanied by predicted inhibition constants of 406.72 nM and 318.21 nM, intermolecular energies of −8.72 kcal/mol and −10.60 kcal/mol, and surface contact areas of 866.97 Å2 and 946.67 Å2, respectively. Meanwhile, the smaller phenolic and alkaloidal molecules displayed moderate binding energies: Ellagic acid scored −7.04 kcal/mol with a Ki of 6.89 μM; Grandisines reached −6.89 kcal/mol with a Ki of 8.89 μM; Elaeocarpine yielded −6.86 kcal/mol with a Ki of 9.44 μM; and Quercetin showed −6.43 kcal/mol with a Ki of 19.38 μM. These smaller scaffolds generated comparatively compact total interaction surfaces, measuring 592.17 Å2 for Ellagic acid, 635.61 Å2 for Elaeocarpine, 642.93 Å2 for Quercetin, and 679.77 Å2 for Grandisines, alongside modest electrostatic contributions between −0.01 and −0.33 kcal/mol. Detailed examination of the simulated binding poses revealed distinct amino-acid engagement profiles across the catalytic site and neighboring substrate-recognition residues, which include Leu27, Gly143, His163, His164, Met165, Glu166, Pro168, and His172. Stigmasterol engaged the highest number of predefined core residues, forming seven contacts across Phe140, Asn142, Gly143, Cys145, His163, Met165, Glu166, Pro168, His172, Gln189, and Gln192, directly interacting with catalytic residue Cys145 although lacking contact with His41. Both β-Sitosterol and Grandisines engaged six core residues; β-Sitosterol contacted Leu27, His41, Met49, Asn142, Ser144, Cys145, Met165, Glu166, Pro168, and Gln189, whereas Grandisines contacted His41, Met49, Tyr54, Gly143, Cys145, His163, Met165, Glu166, and Gln189, allowing both compounds to contact both catalytic dyad partners simultaneously. Rutin, Cycloeucalenol, and Quercetin each established contacts with five core residues. Rutin engaged Thr25, Leu27, His41, Phe140, Asn142, Ser144, Cys145, His163, Met165, and Gln189, successfully spanning both His41 and Cys145 within the active site. Cycloeucalenol contacted Thr25, Leu27, His41, Met49, Asn142, Cys145, Met165, Pro168, and Gln192, also engaging both catalytic residues. Conversely, Quercetin contacted His41, Phe140, Asn142, His163, Met165, Glu166, His172, and Gln189, interacting with His41 while omitting contact with Cys145. For the remaining molecules, Elaeocarpine and Ellagic acid each engaged four core residues, with both ligands contacting both His41 and Cys145, while Friedelin established three core residue interactions encompassing Thr25, His41, Asn142, Cys145, Met165, and Gln189. The study highlights how distinct chemical architectures achieve affinity through complementary energetic mechanisms. In the comparison between Quercetin and its glycoside Rutin, the addition of a disaccharide moiety expands Rutin’s polar functionality to ten hydrogen-bond donors and sixteen acceptors, allowing extensive multipoint polar interactions that yield a substantially more negative docking score than Quercetin’s compact aglycone core. In sharp contrast, the sterols Stigmasterol and β-Sitosterol possess only one hydrogen-bond donor and one acceptor, relying instead on hydrophobic packing, van der Waals forces, and large non-polar contact surfaces to achieve favorable docking energetics within the protease cavity. The authors emphasize critical methodological limitations inherent to docking simulations. Computational docking scores and AutoDock-calculated inhibition constants represent static energetic estimates rather than direct measurements of biochemical enzyme inhibition or antiviral efficacy. Furthermore, high predicted target affinity does not account for pharmacokinetic hurdles; Rutin’s molecular weight and high hydrogen-bonding count exceed Lipinski Rule-of-Five thresholds, presenting challenges for oral bioavailability and membrane permeability. Because the investigation evaluated a rigid crystal receptor without dynamic simulation, the authors conclude that molecular dynamics trajectories, MM-PBSA or MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations, in vitro enzymatic inhibition assays, ADME profiling, and cell-based viral replication studies remain necessary to determine whether any of these prioritized botanical scaffolds possess genuine therapeutic utility. (Arkansas Democrat-Gazette/Stephen Swofford) Philander Smith University announced this week that it has shifted to virtual instruction “following a limited number of COVID-19 cases.” In-person classes are expected to resume next Monday, the historically Black university in Little Rock said in a social media post on Tuesday. Activities scheduled from Monday onward will proceed, the post says. Homecoming activities through Sunday are canceled except for an outdoor 5K on Saturday, which will occur with health precautions, the post says. Participants from the campus community will be asked to test, according to the post. Rafael Escalera Montoto rescalera@adgnewsroom.com Rafael is a crime and breaking news reporter at the Arkansas Democrat Gazette. He has also covered housing, education, business and other topics at The Baltimore Banner. records.content: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia skip to main content skip to footer Search Expand Menu About Us Our People Education Banking Careers Calendar of Events The Economy Expand Sub-Topics Monetary Policy Banking & Financial Markets Macroeconomics Regional Economics Consumer Finance Expand Sub-Topics Payment Systems Consumer Credit Education Finance Mortgage Markets Community Development Expand Sub-Topics Inclusive Growth Credit & Capital Housing & Neighborhoods Workforce & Economic Development SURVEYS & DATA Expand Sub-Topics REAL-TIME DATA RESEARCH Regional Economic Analysis CONSUMER FINANCE DATA COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DATA Search Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia The Economy How Did the U.S. Policy Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic Affect Inflation and Economic Growth? Article How Did the U.S. Policy Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic Affect Inflation and Economic Growth? 03 Nov ’26 Research in Focus — Fiscal transfers during the pandemic averted a depression-scale collapse at the cost of higher inflation rates, but supply-side disruptions explain most of the inflation surge. Share U.S. inflation has recently spiked to levels not seen since the 1970s. Economists have sought to understand the causes of this unexpected surge, which followed the COVID-19 pandemic.1 The U.S. government’s immediate response to the economic collapse caused by the pandemic was a series of fiscal transfers in 2020–2021 that included the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act; the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act; and the American Rescue Plan. These fiscal transfers together amounted to 11 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2019 dollars. What was the impact of these enormous transfer payments on the macroeconomy? For their paper “Are Fiscal Transfers Inflationary?” Jonas Arias and Minchul Shin of the Philadelphia Fed and Juan Rubio-Ramírez of Emory University and the Atlanta Fed (as well as a visiting scholar at the Philadelphia Fed) studied the evolution of the U.S. economy during the pandemic with a particular emphasis on the role played by fiscal transfers in determining the dynamics of inflation and output. Using a recently developed econometric framework, they examined how key macroeconomic indicators interacted with each other and responded to unexpected shocks over time, how effective fiscal transfers were and at what cost in terms of inflation, and the role that monetary policy played in shaping macroeconomic outcomes.2 The authors used an econometric model, technically known as a rotation-invariant time-varying structural vector autoregression, to quantify the main forces behind changes in the economy.3 In particular, their framework allowed them to disentangle the contributions to output growth and inflation from fiscal transfer shocks; from demand shocks (resulting from, for example, the economywide shutdown early in the pandemic); and from monetary policy shocks from unexpected policy rate adjustments, which affect borrowing costs. They also studied supply shocks — specifically, those stemming from global supply chain shortages — as well as cost-push-related supply shocks. They found that demand shocks initially had a negative impact on both output and the price level as private spending collapsed in 2020. Later, some positive demand shocks occurred from, for example, pent-up demand following the lockdown. This pent-up demand boosted output and reversed the downward pressure on the price level exerted by the spending collapse at the onset of the pandemic. But overall, these demand shocks were not meaningful contributors to inflation during the pandemic — although they did contribute to the rise in short-term interest rates during the recovery phase. Meanwhile, they found that monetary policy shocks overall caused prices to be lower than they otherwise would have been. (This is because the effective lower bound on interest rates left the monetary authorities little room to lower rates further to stimulate the economy.) Postpandemic fiscal transfer shocks, however, significantly lifted output and accounted for a sizable share of the inflation that occurred through mid-2021. These payments dramatically improved economic activity, but this effect was short-lived, with their contribution to GDP diminishing by the end of 2021. The transfers raised the GDP deflator (which measures the price level) by 5 percent in 2021 alone and continued to contribute significantly to the price level through the end of 2024. Even so, fiscal transfers were not the main driver of the price level surge. It was instead the supply shocks that occurred from 2021 onward, reflecting widespread global supply bottlenecks and disruptions in logistics, that contributed the most to inflation and also negatively affected output. To cite just one example, supply-side price pressures mounted because of the global semiconductor chip shortage, creating supply chain disruptions for many U.S. manufacturing industries. Cost-push supply shocks further contributed to inflation, including through product price markups. How did monetary policy influence macroeconomic conditions during the pandemic? Early in the pandemic, monetary policy was contractionary, as the effective lower bound prevented the Federal Reserve from reducing the federal funds rate below zero in the first half of 2020. This contractionary policy weighed on output and the price level. Thereafter, the monetary policy response was expansionary because, through the lens of the econometric framework, the Federal Reserve delayed raising interest rates. Even so, this delayed response was not enough to make monetary policy’s overall contribution to the price level positive during the pandemic era. To learn more about the role of monetary policy in shaping how the expansion of fiscal transfers propagated through the economy, the authors compared the monetary policy response to fiscal transfer shocks during the pandemic with the response during the Great Recession (2007–2009). During the Great Recession, fiscal transfers were about one-quarter of those during the pandemic, and output contracted sharply. Meanwhile, the monetary policy response was systematic and strong, preventing significant inflation, although at the cost of providing weaker support for output. In contrast, a more muted policy response occurred following the pandemic, amplifying the output effects of the transfers but failing to prevent the fiscal transfer shocks from fueling inflation. Using counterfactual analysis, the authors replaced the Great Recession’s fiscal shocks with the large transfers from the pandemic and found that prices would still have risen, but more modestly than during the pandemic. This is because interest rates would have increased much more during the Great Recession as a result of systematic monetary policy adjustments.4 Their findings underscore that monetary policy plays a critical role in how fiscal transfers impact the macroeconomy. They conclude that, despite the unwanted inflation, U.S. fiscal transfers during the pandemic were essential in preventing an output collapse similar to the one experienced during the Great Depression. Without these transfers, real GDP per capita would have fallen by over 20 percent, rivaling the decline during the early 1930s. The cost of these transfers has been a sizable increase in the price level through mid-2021 with diminishing but persistent positive contributions to the price level through the end of 2024. The views expressed here are solely those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia or the Federal Reserve System. See, for example, Olivier Blanchard and Ben Bernanke, “What Caused the U.S. Pandemic-Era Inflation?” National Bureau of Economic Research Working Paper 31417 (2023), https://doi.org/10.3386/w31417. They extended the methodology introduced in the paper they wrote with Daniel Waggoner, “Inference Based on Time-Varying SVARs Identified with Sign Restrictions,” Review of Economic Studies (forthcoming). Their framework contains six key variables: fiscal transfers relative to GDP; real output growth per capita; the GDP deflator; the one-year Treasury yield, which captures changes in the policy rate and adjustments to the Federal Reserve’s balance sheet; the Institute for Supply Management Manufacturing Supplier Deliveries Index, which captures delivery delays; and the personal savings rate, which reflects households’ marginal decisions between spending and saving in response to fiscal transfers. They emphasize that “identifying the causal effects of fiscal transfers requires separating exogenous policy innovations [that is, unplanned interventions] from systematic policy responses [that is, standard rule-like adjustments] to macroeconomic conditions.”

records.content: 东南亚地区Long COVID定义、疾病负担、诊断与管理的改良Delphi共识:区域临床实践与卫生政策框架 《Pulmonary Therapy》:Long COVID: A Modified Delphi Consensus on Definition, Burden, Diagnosis and Management in Southeast Asia 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月08日 来源:Pulmonary Therapy 3.4 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Original Research Open access 引言 长COVID(Long COVID)是一种异质性感染后状态,发生于急性严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)感染后。围绕其定义、疾病负担、诊断和管理的持续不确定性,使东南亚地区的临床识别和照护复杂化。方法 研究人员在来自六个东南亚国家的十二名专家中开展了一项改良Delphi(德尔菲)共识研究,以制定关于长COVID的区域性指导。共识预先定义为≥80%一致,即12名专家中至少10名在多项选择题中选择相同回答,或在Likert(李克特)量表问题上表示同意(例如同意/强烈同意,最重要/更重要,相关/高度相关)。达到共识的问题从后续轮次中删除,未解决问题则修订、合并或扩展。在最后一轮中,对未达到共识的Likert量表问题采用事后描述性类别“中等支持”,以五点重要性量表(“最重要”至“最不重要”)中的“重要”作为中点类别,以捕捉被认为重要但未达到共识阈值的回答。结果 所有“定义”“疾病负担”和“管理”主题问题以及大多数“诊断”问题均达到共识。专家将长COVID定义为SARS-CoV-2感染后持续>3个月且无法解释的症状,区别于急性COVID-19后状态(post-acute COVID-19),且无最低严重程度阈值要求。长COVID被认为影响约6%–10%的SARS-CoV-2感染后个体,与已发表的世界卫生组织(WHO)和韩国感染病学会(KSID)估计一致;建议通过临床评估和症状导向检测进行诊断。急性COVID-19期间住院被确定为发生长COVID的危险因素。专家建议多学科、症状导向照护、康复、活动节律管理(pacing)和随访。疫苗接种和再感染预防被支持作为重要的长COVID风险降低策略,并且对于高风险个体,应考虑早期抗病毒治疗以预防严重急性疾病和住院。对于诊断所需的既往病史未达到共识;对加强针状态、缺乏早期抗病毒治疗、COVID前健康评估和标准化患者报告结局工具观察到中等支持。结论 该Delphi研究为东南亚长COVID提供了实用的区域性共识框架。 研究背景:急性SARS-CoV-2感染后持续症状自2020年中受到关注,2020年ICD编码和2021年WHO临床病例定义发布后逐步获得正式认可。但主要卫生机构对长COVID(Long COVID,SARS-CoV-2感染后持续症状)的定义仍存在明显差异:WHO要求症状在感染后3个月内出现并持续至少2个月;英国国家卫生与临床优化研究所(NICE)区分“ongoing symptomatic COVID-19”(4–12周)与“post-COVID-19 syndrome”(超过12周);美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)和美国国家科学院、工程院和医学院(NASEM)将其定义为感染后至少3个月的慢性状态;KSID(韩国感染病学会)和马来西亚卫生部则描述为诊断后超过3个月无法解释的症状。上述定义未统一要求实验室确认,未规定最低症状严重度或功能受损阈值,持续时间亦不一致,影响临床识别、研究可比性和治疗规划。多数长COVID患病率数据来自高收入国家,而亚洲及东南亚支持系统可能存在缺口,区域识别不足且具体行动有限;已有Delphi共识未针对亚洲定制。因此,研究人员开展区域改良Delphi共识研究,以形成东南亚长COVID定义、疾病负担、诊断和管理建议,指导临床实践并为卫生政策提供依据。 领取义翘神州针对Omicron的一站式解决方案 领 取 研究开展及意义:研究人员采用改良Delphi(德尔菲,多轮匿名专家共识方法),纳入来自新加坡、印度尼西亚、马来西亚、菲律宾、泰国和越南的12名专家,开展两轮匿名封闭式在线问卷。专家组包括5名感染病专家(41.7%)和7名呼吸科医师(58.3%);8名具有超过20年经验,4名具有10–20年经验。研究得出区域性共识框架,有助于减少定义和诊疗不一致,促进临床识别、研究可比性和患者照护;对长COVID识别不足且正式指导有限的东南亚具有现实意义,并强调评估、康复和支持服务的公平可及。 关键技术方法(不超过250字):研究采用改良Delphi共识法,基于2024—2025年PubMed和Google Scholar文献检索(关键词含Long COVID、post-COVID-19 condition、post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection、Asia、SEA,并更新至2026年4月)设计匿名封闭式在线问卷。12名专家来自新加坡、印度尼西亚、马来西亚、菲律宾、泰国和越南六国,均具COVID-19管理专长。共识阈值预设为≥80%(12名中至少10名选择预设上端类别)。第一轮(2025年10—12月)评估26个实质问题,第二轮(2026年2—3月)评估6个未共识问题及1个新增问题;达到阈值条目删除,未解决条目修订、合并或扩展。末轮对未达阈值Likert条目事后采用“中等支持”描述,仅作描述不作共识。研究按CREDES和ACCORD报告,问卷匿名实施。 研究结果:Theme 1:Definition(定义)。通过两轮改良Delphi问卷,定义主题全部条目达成共识(10–12/12,83.3%–100%):长COVID为SARS-CoV-2感染后超过3个月、无法由其他诊断解释的症状,区别于post-acute COVID-19(4周至3个月),且不设最低症状严重度门槛;其中症状起始和持续时间11/12(91.7%)、病例定义12/12(100%)、与post-acute COVID-19区别11/12(91.7%)、不规定最低症状严重度10/12(83.3%)。Theme 2:Burden(疾病负担)。第一轮负担主题全部问题达成共识。专家组以10/12(83.3%)认可长COVID约占急性SARS-CoV-2感染者的6%–10%,该范围为对WHO约6%和KSID 10%已发表估计的认可,并非东南亚实测患病率;共识认为其影响所有年龄和社会经济背景,但35–65岁和低收入群体负担更重,约五分之一受影响者症状严重;长COVID对日常功能和经济生产力造成挑战,原文引用日本2024年720亿美元生产力损失及台湾120亿美元、相当于GDP 1.5%的损失;泰国337名既往感染者中32.9%发生长COVID,焦虑28.5%、疲劳26.1%、呼吸困难13.4%常见;越南1507名12–17岁儿童中5.6%符合WHO标准,记忆下降85.9%、注意力差58.8%、疲劳57.6%常见,并伴学业中断和缺勤增加;12/12(100%)认为需要证据化政策、临床与公众教育及专门资源。Theme 3:Diagnosis(诊断)。多数诊断问题达成共识。专家组认为长COVID可累及任何器官系统,疲劳、运动后不适、认知障碍和气短常见,文献记录相关症状超过200种;目前无验证性生物标志物,诊断主要依赖临床评估和患者病史,检查用于评估并发症和共病而非确认长COVID;专科长COVID门诊评估应包括急性感染史、工作/家庭/社会领域功能影响及症状变化监测,COVID前健康状态评估和标准化患者报告结局工具C19-YRSm(改良COVID-19约克郡康复量表)仅获中等支持(均由8/12、66.7%升至含中点12/12、100%);症状导向实验室检测和专科转诊用于排除替代诊断。风险分层方面,未及时更新COVID-19疫苗接种和急性COVID-19期间住院为发生长COVID的危险因素达成共识;其他危险因素包括既往慢性病、高体质指数(BMI)、严重急性COVID-19、感染时未接种疫苗和重复SARS-CoV-2感染。专家组未就诊断是否必须依据临床或需有SARS-CoV-2聚合酶链反应(PCR)/快速抗原检测(RAT)阳性记录达成共识;约30%感染可能无症状。缺乏早期抗病毒治疗(8/12,66.7%;含中点10/12,83.3%)和加强针逾期(4/12,33.3%;含中点10/12,83.3%)仅为中等支持。Theme 4:Management(管理)。管理主题达成共识:长COVID无单一获批药物治疗,需个体化、症状导向管理。症状治疗共识包括:持续呼吸困难可调整吸入剂剂量或采用疾病特异治疗;慢性感染后咳嗽可用抗组胺药和鼻内糖皮质激素;原发性头痛在排除继发原因后对症治疗;嗅觉障碍采用嗅觉训练联合局部糖皮质激素鼻喷剂;不明原因疲劳在排除其他原因后以康复治疗为一线;睡眠障碍应消除干扰因素并处理病因;焦虑或抑郁需精神科转诊以排除其他原因,严重精神症状或自伤风险应立即咨询。康复与随访方面,共识支持由单一临床医生进行规律长期随访、向患者解释诊断和预后、以症状导向的活动节律管理(pacing)优于常规渐进运动,并可考虑常规使用17项C19-YRS。预防方面,共识支持对有症状、非住院高风险急性COVID-19个体考虑早期使用获批抗病毒药以预防重症和住院;目前无抗病毒药被正式批准专门预防长COVID,但急性期5天内使用现有口服抗病毒药可能降低长COVID风险;共识支持按推荐接种COVID-19疫苗包括加强针,以及在拥挤室内环境佩戴合适口罩、手卫生、咳嗽礼仪和良好室内通风。 讨论部分总结:该共识认为统一定义对临床识别、研究可比性和治疗规划具有及时意义;6%–10%负担范围为区域规划和宣传的参考带,而非东南亚实测值;诊断在缺乏生物标志物时以临床评估和病史为主,C19-YRSm等工具仅中等支持;管理强调多学科、症状导向、康复、pacing和长期随访,预防强调疫苗、再感染预防和早期抗病毒治疗。局限性包括:12名专家仅来自东南亚11国中的6国,部分卫生系统结构不同国家未覆盖;建议应主要在参与国家情境中解释;专科康复、初级保健、心血管、神经、精神或职业医学代表未纳入;两个第一轮危险因素子问题(女性性别和急性期休息不足)未再调查;疾病流行病学仍在演变,负担估计多来自早期大流行阶段和未/部分接种队列。 研究结论部分译文:该Delphi共识研究为改善东南亚长COVID照护提供了及时且可操作的框架,作为该地区的区域指导而非普适性指导。通过在定义、疾病负担、诊断和管理等核心领域达成一致,该研究有助于减少可能阻碍临床识别、研究可比性和患者照护的现有不一致。其结果对长COVID仍被低估且正式指导有限的地区尤其相关。研究结果还强调需要公平获得评估、康复和支持服务,尤其对脆弱人群。同时,未达成共识和中等支持的领域表明证据基础仍不完整,需要进一步研究以完善风险分层、诊断工具和专科门诊评估。 3:Diagnosis(诊断)。多数诊断问题达成共识。专家组认为长COVID可累及任何器官系统,疲劳、运动后不适、认知障碍和气短常见,文献记录相关症状超过200种;目前无验证性生物标志物,诊断主要依赖临床评估和患者病史,检查用于评估并发症和共病而非确认长COVID;专科长COVID门诊评估应包括急性感染史、工作/家庭/社会领域功能影响及症状变化监测,COVID前健康状态评估和标准化患者报告结局工具C19-YRSm(改良COVID-19约克郡康复量表)仅获中等支持(均由8/12、66.7%升至含中点12/12、100%);症状导向实验室检测和专科转诊用于排除替代诊断。风险分层方面,未及时更新COVID-19疫苗接种和急性COVID-19期间住院为发生长COVID的危险因素达成共识;其他危险因素包括既往慢性病、高体质指数(BMI)、严重急性COVID-19、感染时未接种疫苗和重复SARS-CoV-2感染。专家组未就诊断是否必须依据临床或需有SARS-CoV-2聚合酶链反应(PCR)/快速抗原检测(RAT)阳性记录达成共识;约30%感染可能无症状。缺乏早期抗病毒治疗(8/12,66.7%;含中点10/12,83.3%)和加强针逾期(4/12,33.3%;含中点10/12,83.3%)仅为中等支持。Theme 4:Management(管理)。管理主题达成共识:长COVID无单一获批药物治疗,需个体化、症状导向管理。症状治疗共识包括:持续呼吸困难可调整吸入剂剂量或采用疾病特异治疗;慢性感染后咳嗽可用抗组胺药和鼻内糖皮质激素;原发性头痛在排除继发原因后对症治疗;嗅觉障碍采用嗅觉训练联合局部糖皮质激素鼻喷剂;不明原因疲劳在排除其他原因后以康复治疗为一线;睡眠障碍应消除干扰因素并处理病因;焦虑或抑郁需精神科转诊以排除其他原因,严重精神症状或自伤风险应立即咨询。康复与随访方面,共识支持由单一临床医生进行规律长期随访、向患者解释诊断和预后、以症状导向的活动节律管理(pacing)优于常规渐进运动,并可考虑常规使用17项C19-YRS。预防方面,共识支持对有症状、非住院高风险急性COVID-19个体考虑早期使用获批抗病毒药以预防重症和住院;目前无抗病毒药被正式批准专门预防长COVID,但急性期5天内使用现有口服抗病毒药可能降低长COVID风险;共识支持按推荐接种COVID-19疫苗包括加强针,以及在拥挤室内环境佩戴合适口罩、手卫生、咳嗽礼仪和良好室内通风。讨论部分总结:该共识认为统一定义对临床识别、研究可比性和治疗规划具有及时意义;6%–10%负担范围为区域规划和宣传的参考带,而非东南亚实测值;诊断在缺乏生物标志物时以临床评估和病史为主,C19-YRSm等工具仅中等支持;管理强调多学科、症状导向、康复、pacing和长期随访,预防强调疫苗、再感染预防和早期抗病毒治疗。局限性包括:12名专家仅来自东南亚11国中的6国,部分卫生系统结构不同国家未覆盖;建议应主要在参与国家情境中解释;专科康复、初级保健、心血管、神经、精神或职业医学代表未纳入;两个第一轮危险因素子问题(女性性别和急性期休息不足)未再调查;疾病流行病学仍在演变,负担估计多来自早期大流行阶段和未/部分接种队列。研究结论部分译文:该Delphi共识研究为改善东南亚长COVID照护提供了及时且可操作的框架,作为该地区的区域指导而非普适性指导。通过在定义、疾病负担、诊断和管理等核心领域达成一致,该研究有助于减少可能阻碍临床识别、研究可比性和患者照护的现有不一致。其结果对长COVID仍被低估且正式指导有限的地区尤其相关。研究结果还强调需要公平获得评估、康复和支持服务,尤其对脆弱人群。同时,未达成共识和中等支持的领域表明证据基础仍不完整,需要进一步研究以完善风险分层、诊断工具和专科门诊评估。 records.content_title: Omicron a 'different foe' that needs new plan: Ardern
records.content: Most who catch omicron will recover at home, thanks to high vaccination rates, says Ardern. (Image: Getty) Prime minister Jacinda Ardern begins the political new year in earnest with the announcement of the “new plan” required to combat the inevitable spread of the highly transmissible omicron variant of covid-19 through the New Zealand population. In opening remarks to the Labour party’s caucus retreat at a coastal resort south of New Plymouth, Ardern said omicron was a “different foe”. “Now we will experience cases in New Zealand at a level we haven’t experienced before.” However, most cases would recover at home because high vaccination rates would reduce the severity of illness for most who contracted the virus. They were her most explicit comments yet about the extent to which NZ’s previous approaches to covid – elimination and then suppression – will not work once omicron gets into the community. Two further cases of omicron have been confirmed in the community in Auckland overnight, with Auckland district health board documents leaked to Māori TV estimating that once omicron becomes established in NZ, total daily cases of around 50,000 can be expected over a 12-to-16 week outbreak. With Ardern and covid response minister Chris Hipkins already conceding omicron will become established, the prime minister said the latest variant represented a “different challenge” to previous variants. While NZ had suppressed the prevalence of the delta covid variant better than many other countries and was among the most highly vaccinated populations in the world, omicron was a “different foe” and there were likely to be more variants after omicron. She rallied her caucus troops saying she felt resolute and confident, particularly because the approach to delta had worked and given New Zealanders a summer holiday, while the rollout of boosters and vaccination for five-to-11 year-olds was putting NZ in a position that many other countries were not in. “This time last year, we were not vaccinated,” she said. Now, as well as vaccination, there were anti-viral drugs becoming available. Ardern is expected to announce any changes to the so-called ‘traffic light’ covid protection system this afternoon, with the only likely move being a possible reduction in the ‘red’ status of the Northland region falling to orange. However, of greater significance will be the detail of announcements that are expected to cover how the government will approach the almost inevitable omicron surge. Hipkins yesterday would not be drawn ahead of a cabinet discussion yesterday afternoon, but acknowledged the concern that there could be very high levels of workers off work during the outbreak, that it was a matter of judgement as to whether to let the virus peak fast or try to spread out its impact, and that the need for MIQ for arrivals from offshore could be greatly reduced once the virus was established here. Among considerations is the extent to which the timing of the outbreak can be ‘controlled’ to occur in late summer rather than drifting into winter, when it would coincide with the winter flu season and potentially put greater strain on the public health system. records.content_title: Twin-Based Study Helps Characterize Long COVID | Physicians Weekly
records.content: Many questions about COVID-19 outcomes remain unanswered. While there are several risk factors researchers have identified for negative outcomes, there is still a lack of evidence for why patients who seemingly lack these risk factors experience severe outcomes, including long COVID. Twin-Based Study Helps Characterize Long COVID To develop a better understanding of factors that may influence the development of long COVID in particular, Tom Quach, a medical student at Stanford University in San Francisco, California, and colleagues conducted a study to characterize long COVID among twins. They presented their findings at IDWeek in Washington, DC, this year. Conducting a Twin-Based Long COVID Study Quach and colleagues conducted an exploratory, cross-sectional study with pairs of twins participating in the Stanford Twin Research Registry (TRR). Their goal was “to assess the clinical impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection burden between monozygotic (MZ) and dizygotic (DZ) twins and compare with non-twin long COVID patients.” All study participants were aged 18 and older. The researchers adapted the REDCap questionnaire for long COVID care and disseminated it to study participants. They compared demographics, symptoms, functional status, symptom duration, and concordance versus discordance between the twin pairs and the non-twin long COVID cohorts. Twins and Nontwins Report Different Outcomes The twin cohort had a mean age of 45.8 years, was 84.1% female and 87.8% white, and had a mean symptom duration of 1,443 days. Most (60.5%) had no comorbid conditions, and 91% were vaccinated. Even so, 15% of the twin cohort developed long COVID symptoms. Among the twins, only two pairs experienced concordance of long COVID symptoms. Interestingly, 50.6% of the twins had incapacitating functional status, compared with 81.9% of the nontwin cohort. The twin cohort also reported less severe symptoms than the nontwin cohort. Quach and colleagues suggest that “integration of proteomics and immunophenotypic profiling of twins from this and other long COVID twin cohorts may help identify molecular pathways and the pathobiology of long COVID, which in turn may provide further insight into novel treatment methods.” References Quach T, et al. Image for illustration purposes Texas Border Business - Advertisement - U.S. Department of Justice A federal grand jury in the Central District of California returned an indictment yesterday charging Marisela Nuno, 53, of Los Angeles, California, with an $18 million scheme to defraud the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and the Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program, federal stimulus programs authorized as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act. According to court documents, the defendant allegedly obtained funds under the PPP and EIDL program by submitting false and fraudulent loan applications that collectively sought over $15.7 million in PPP funds and over $2.6 million in EIDL funds. The defendant is alleged to have submitted applications on behalf of businesses and entities she purportedly owned, knowing that the applications contained materially false statements and misrepresentations concerning, among other things, the purported entities’ number of employees, average monthly payroll, gross revenues, and eligibility for funding. - Advertisement - The defendant also is alleged to have submitted materially false supporting tax documentation with the applications. The defendant then allegedly used the loan funds for purposes not authorized by the PPP or the EIDL program, including for the purchase of private property, business startup costs, and payments to family members. Nuno is charged with three counts of wire fraud and one count of money laundering. If convicted, she faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on each count of wire fraud, and 10 years in prison on the count of money laundering. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division); Special Agent in Charge Robert Molvar of the FBI’s Criminal Division; Special Agent in Charge Darren Lian of the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division (IRS CI) Los Angeles Field Office, Special Agent in Charge Timothy Larson of the U.S. Small Business Administration Office of Inspector General (SBA OIG) made the announcement. The FBI Los Angeles Field Office, IRS CI, and SBA OIG investigated the case. - Advertisement - Trial Attorney Ariel Glasner of the Fraud Division’s Public Trust and Financial Integrity Section and Trial Attorney Edward Emokpae of the Criminal Division’s White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section are prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. An indictment is merely an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Jacob Michael Laufenberg, age 36, from Dubuque, received the sentence after pleading guilty to wire fraud on February 23. According to sentencing hearings, in May 2020, Laufenberg applied for unemployment benefits in Iowa. He then ended up receiving those benefits in April 2021. While he was receiving unemployment benefits, he concealed his employment with two employers and the fact that he was incarcerated in a county jail for nearly two months. Because of his false statements about his employment and custody status cause him to receive unemployment funds that he was not entitled to get. In addition to Laufenberg’s more than 2 years in federal prison, he was also ordered to make $17,102 in restitution to Iowa Workforce Development. He must also serve a five-year term of supervised released after the prison term. Laufenberg is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison. from COVID-19 includes regular trips to Pittsburgh From 2021 to 2024, UPMC performed eight such transplants, and Dennis Franklin so far is the longest surviving. Hanna Webster Pittsburgh Post-Gazette hwebster@post-gazette.com Nov 6, 2026 9:00 AM Lounging on an outside patio in Shadyside on a recent October afternoon, Dennis Franklin heard the roar of a helicopter landing across the street at UPMC Shadyside Hospital. He was snapped back to his stay in Pittsburgh nearly five years earlier, when he was recovering from a double lung transplant. “I used to hear them all the time,” he recalled. “They’re either bringing in a patient or an organ for somebody.” A healthy and active 59-year-old, Franklin got COVID-19 the summer of 2021 and quickly became weaker. His lungs were so infected and scarred from the virus that they had stiffened, and he could barely breathe. Living in Missouri at the time, and now based in Illinois, Franklin took a 10-hour ambulance ride to UPMC that December for the transplant that would save his life. Advertisement The now-65-year-old can walk, talk, drive and breathe — activities he could not do on his own five years ago, just before doctors gave him the lungs of a 17-year-old donor. Having survived a double lung transplant and COVID, Franklin is part of a small group of patients doctors are just beginning to understand. This cohort is approaching its five-year survival mark, where scientists can begin to examine how these COVID transplant patients are faring — and how survival rates compare to other types of lung transplantation, as with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD. “When we first started doing lung transplants with COVID, it was unclear whether that was a good idea,” said Joseph Pilewski, Franklin’s physician and associate chief in the division of pulmonary, allergy, critical care and sleep medicine at the University of Pittsburgh. “Their outcomes look to be relatively similar, but they tend to have more complications early.” Advertisement While there’s ample research on outcomes for other lung transplant patients, no research study on the five-year outcomes of COVID lung transplant patients yet exists. From 2021 to 2024, UPMC performed eight of these transplants, and Franklin so far is the longest surviving. Pilewski only has the reference of general lung transplant recipients, but many of them have fared as well as Franklin, he said. “They’re living 10 to 15 years after their transplant; they get to see kids or grandkids grow up and do things they otherwise wouldn’t have been able to,” Pilewski said. “It’s really remarkable.” Franklin and his wife, Julia Renshaw-Franklin, flew to Pittsburgh the week of Oct. 20 for his five-year checkup with his care team. Transplant patients receive routine follow-ups to monitor their progress and make sure their bodies are not rejecting the new organs. During these appointments, Franklin undergoes a breathing test and physical exam, plus bloodwork and imaging of his lungs. He also gets monthly bloodwork to measure his blood oxygen, hemoglobin and white blood cell count. Pilewski said he has no concerns. “I’ve seen Dennis several times a year since before his surgery, and he’s made a very nice recovery from a very complicated journey,” Pilewski said. “He has been able to do a lot with his life.” But, for Franklin, it took longer to recover than he anticipated, and he reached a point last year where he thought he had plateaued. He could breathe fine, but his stamina was shot and he was lethargic. He took frequent breaks after 10 or 20 minutes of walking. “I was in the mindset of, ‘This is my new norm. I’ll live with it, because the other option is, I didn’t make it, so I’m happy with what I got,’” he said. Then he noticed he was getting stronger. He got a gym membership and began walking on the treadmill more. His wife got sick, and he stepped up to take care of her. “It just seemed like it was the time for me to get better,” Franklin said. The procedure has, of course, changed his life and introduced new limitations. Compared to patients with chronic lung disease, COVID patients who need a double lung transplant may not have the time or the presence of mind to consider the risks and benefits of transplantation, so it can be more jarring. Getting the procedure will tie them to long-term medical care and immunosuppressant drugs. Franklin takes these drugs to avoid organ rejection, which leaves him at a higher risk of infection. Because of this, the Franklins don’t go to movie theaters or concerts anymore. He contracted respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in February; his symptoms were severe and took months to ameliorate. He also has kidney failure from an acute injury, related to the contrast dye that surgeons used during the procedure and imaging tests, requiring dialysis three times a week. A post-op gangrene infection led to the amputation of half his index finger. “The biggest impediment for him has been the kidney function,” said Pilewski. “It’s a bit of an inconvenience and a time investment.” Franklin isn’t bothered by it. He attributes his success in part to gratitude and a positive attitude, and he’s had the privilege of growing close to two of his grandchildren, who were born while he was in the hospital. “I can’t complain about anything,” he said. “You can breathe again. I mean, I couldn't breathe, period, beforehand.” This perspective shift is common for double lung transplant patients, said Namrata Patel, clinical director of the interstitial lung disease program at Penn Medicine and a physician. Patel was not involved in Franklin’s care but has performed lung transplants on coronavirus-ravaged lungs. “Most of my patients live a very full life,” said Patel. “They go back to practicing law and hiking. Even though people can go back to work, they realize the importance of life and the most important priorities in life. They’re willing to make trade-offs. They understand how valuable this gift is for them.” Many choose not to return to work at all, in favor of spending more time with their family. Franklin followed this path. He described his pre-COVID self as a workaholic who often pulled 12-hour days at his job as a Staples delivery driver. While his coworkers left at 5 p.m., he’d work until all the deliveries were unloaded from his truck. Patel and her team at Penn Medicine have performed around 25 double lung transplants for COVID patients, the peak of those procedures being in 2021, the year Franklin received his. She’s noticed this cohort is doing as well as patients who get lung transplants for lung disease, although some face earlier complications. “The patient survival rate is good,” she said. “It’s more the process of getting back to their life.” Pilewski noted there have been advances in the science of organ preservation, and transplant surgeons have learned a lot during the pandemic, which could contribute to better outcomes for transplant patients in the future. But he stressed that there’s still a shortage of organs, and many die while on the waiting list. “It’s important for the public to understand the benefits of organ donation,” said Pilewski. “People with kidney failure can go on dialysis, but the shortage for hearts, lungs and liver is significant.” First Published: November 6, 2026, 9:00 a.m. Hanna Webster has covered health for the Post-Gazette since 2022, specializing in health equity and the opioid crisis. The review notes that aging-related immune decline, co-occurring chronic conditions, and frailty increase susceptibility to respiratory viruses, reduce vaccine-induced immune responses, and contribute to more severe clinical illness. Furthermore, forms of immune compromise such as haematological malignancy, solid organ transplantation, and immunosuppressive therapy further heighten patient vulnerability. Discover more Health health Academic research tools The authors highlight that respiratory viral infections and chronic non-communicable conditions interact bidirectionally. Pre-existing diseases including diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease elevate the risk of severe respiratory infection, while viral infections can destabilize or exacerbate these underlying conditions, leading to functional decline and loss of physiological reserve in frail individuals. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of community-acquired pneumonia cases and can coexist with or predispose older adults to secondary bacterial infections. Among these pathogens, influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 currently represent the principal vaccine-modifiable respiratory viruses in older populations. While the effects of vaccination on infection and other clinical endpoints vary by pathogen, vaccine, and population, the review emphasizes that vaccination consistently offers its strongest protection against severe disease, hospitalization, and mortality. Emerging evidence also indicates potential benefits in limiting chronic disease destabilization and cardiorespiratory complications, suggesting that vaccination serves to alter the overall disease trajectory and prevent downstream loss of physiological reserve. The narrative review published in Aging Clinical and Experimental Research examines viral pneumonia in older adults specifically at the intersection of immunosenescence, frailty, multimorbidity, and immune compromise. The authors emphasize that respiratory viral infections in this older population should not be regarded merely as isolated acute events, but rather as part of a wider vaccine-modifiable clinical burden. According to the review, the interconnected influences of aging-related immune decline, co-occurring chronic conditions, and frailty collectively increase vulnerability to viral respiratory pathogens, reduce the immune responses elicited by vaccination, and contribute to more severe manifestations of disease. Furthermore, the presence of specific forms of additional immune compromise, explicitly including haematological malignancy, solid organ transplantation, and immunosuppressive therapy, serves to heighten this patient vulnerability even further. A central observation in the review is the bidirectional nature of the interaction between respiratory viral infections and underlying non-communicable diseases. The authors report that pre-existing chronic conditions, including diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, markedly increase an individual’s risk of developing severe respiratory infections. Conversely, acquiring a viral infection can precipitate the acute destabilisation or exacerbation of those established underlying diseases. Among frail older adults, the impact of these events frequently extends well beyond the acute infective episode, resulting in subsequent functional decline and a compounding loss of physiological reserve. In the broader context of acute lower respiratory illness, the review notes that respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of community-acquired pneumonia cases, where they can either coexist with bacterial pathogens or predispose affected individuals to secondary bacterial infection. Discover more Biotech startup funding Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Donate to Research In evaluating preventive measures, the authors identify influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as the principal vaccine-modifiable respiratory viral pathogens currently affecting older adults. The review underscores that the protection afforded by vaccination is at its strongest and most consistent when preventing severe disease, hospitalisation, and mortality. In contrast, vaccine-induced protection against initial infection and other clinical endpoints displays variability depending on the specific viral pathogen, the particular vaccine administered, and the characteristics of the targeted population. Beyond traditional acute outcomes, the review highlights emerging evidence suggesting that vaccination can confer clinical benefits that reach past acute respiratory manifestations. Specifically, reported data indicate potential reductions in selected cardiorespiratory complications as well as reductions in chronic disease destabilisation following viral infection. On the basis of these collective findings, the authors propose that vaccination in older adults should be considered not solely as an intervention designed to prevent primary infection, but strategically as a means to modify the broader clinical trajectory of respiratory viral illness. Under this paradigm, modifying the disease trajectory carries the tangible potential to reduce severe clinical outcomes, protect overall health status, and limit the downstream loss of physiological reserve in vulnerable aging individuals. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Sunday, November 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Targeting Host Entry and Cholinergic Pathways Could Blunt Future Viral Pandemics by November 8, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Targeting Host Entry and Cholinergic Pathways Could Blunt Future Viral Pandemics Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A narrative review published in Discover Viruses evaluates universal mechanistic pathways of viral infection to identify accessible interventions that could help blunt future pandemics. Authored by researcher Marco Leitzke, the perspective argues that while vaccine innovation remains vital, comprehensive pandemic preparedness requires integrating strategies that directly disrupt conserved host-pathogen interactions. Drawing on evidence documented during the coronavirus disease 2019 crisis, the review highlights how respiratory viruses exploit shared host enzymes for cellular entry, subvert neuro-immune inflammatory controls, and hijack intracellular replication cascades. By targeting these shared biological vulnerabilities—using approaches ranging from protease inhibitors and cholinergic ligands to simple antiseptic rinses—the author suggests that transmission chains can be suppressed and disease severity curtailed before novel viral variants escape established vaccine defenses. The foundation for this perspective rests on the severe societal and clinical fallout experienced during the global spread of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, which the World Health Organization declared over as a public health emergency on May 5, 2023. Beyond causing acute medical crises, the pandemic imposed immense economic burdens, generating an annual global economic loss of approximately one trillion United States dollars, equivalent to roughly one percent of worldwide economic output. Leitzke emphasizes that the crisis also revealed profound vulnerabilities in social cohesion and institutional trust. Public health responses, while necessary to avert catastrophic hospital collapse as seen in Bergamo and Manaus, fostered sharp social divisions between supporters of interventions and those doubting viral causality. Hostile polarization emerged over vaccination, face masks, and gathering limits, eroding confidence in medical governance and leaving enduring disruptions across communities. Compounding these systemic tensions were the chronic health burdens that emerged following initial infections and mass immunization efforts. The review highlights the substantial prevalence of postviral syndromes, clinically termed long COVID, which in severe presentations can manifest as myalgic encephalomyelitis or chronic fatigue syndrome. Affected patients endure debilitating physical exhaustion and multisystem impairments that remain exceptionally difficult to diagnose paraclinically because medicine lacks validated biomarkers and a fully defined pathogenesis. Similar clinical pictures have been observed following vaccination, creating recognized postvaccination syndromes that pose identical diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Without clear mechanistic explanations for post-acute infection syndromes, standard practice has lacked curative therapies, demonstrating the pressing need to investigate the fundamental biological mechanisms of viral injury. To establish effective defenses against subsequent outbreaks, the analysis examines the prerequisites of pandemic emergence: high human population density, a highly transmissible pathogen, and the absence of rapid spread-prevention measures. In SARS-CoV-2, transmission velocity was accelerated by host enzymatic priming in the upper respiratory tract. Specifically, transmembrane serine protease 2 cleaves the viral spike glycoprotein into distinct S1 and S2 subunits. This enzymatic cleavage increases the binding affinity between the spike protein and human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptors by a factor of ten to fifteen. Consequently, the viral dose required to establish an active infection decreases by that exact same factor. By lowering the infective threshold and speeding cellular entry, this host protease interaction fueled rapid increases in societal viral loads, transforming localized outbreaks into widespread contagion. Once inside host cells, viral virulence is further magnified through the subversion of the nuclear factor kappa B signaling pathway, an innate cellular defense mechanism. Severe COVID-19 presentations frequently resemble bacterial sepsis because viral replication relies directly on this transcription pathway. SARS-CoV-2 stimulates the enzymatic deubiquitination of cytoplasmic nuclear factor kappa B precursors—including p65, p50, p52, c-Rel, RelA, and RelB—mediated by the cellular proteasome and inhibitor of kappa B kinase. This processing causes excessive translocation of these mature subunits into the nucleoplasm. The resulting unrestricted nuclear transcription drives massive production of the virus itself, alongside a surge of proinflammatory cytokines such as tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-1, interleukin-6, and interleukin-8. Concurrently, hypertranscription of prothrombotic tissue factor and antifibrinolytic plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 initiates hypercoagulation, precipitating hypoxic multiorgan failure and severe disease. Under normal physiological conditions, unrestrained inflammatory cascades are arrested by the nervous system through the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, an innate regulatory reflex governed by the vagus nerve. Afferent sensory signals from damaged tissues travel to the nucleus tractus solitarii within the dorsal vagal complex, where impulses are integrated through a central muscarinic network and relayed to downstream vagal centers, including the area postrema and nucleus accumbens. Efferent signals directed from these structures and the dorsal motor vagus nucleus stimulate the localized release of acetylcholine. When released acetylcholine binds to homomeric alpha-7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors on cytokine-synthesizing cells, it halts nuclear factor kappa B activity, suppressing cytokine transcription and preventing tissue destruction. However, SARS-CoV-2 disables this biological brake through a specific proline-arginine-arginine-alanine sequence in its spike glycoprotein, which nonintrinsically adheres to and blocks these nicotinic receptors. This receptor blockade provides a plausible pathophysiological explanation for postviral syndromes like long COVID and chronic fatigue. Beyond homomeric alpha-7 receptors, the viral spike motif also interacts antagonistically with heteromeric nicotinic subtypes, such as alpha-3-beta-2, alpha-4-beta-2, and alpha-9 receptors. Because physical stamina depends heavily on efficient cholinergic transmission, younger and more physically active cohorts experience a markedly higher incidence of long COVID-related fatigue compared to less active or older demographics. Conversely, pediatric patients naturally maintain robust sympathovagal balance, explaining why severe acute progressions are exceptionally rare in children without severe autonomic comorbidities. Restoring vagal signaling through noninvasive vagus nerve stimulation has shown clinical benefits. Furthermore, transcutaneous administration of low-dose nicotine, which binds nicotinic receptors with thirty times greater affinity than the viral spike protein, has shown promising anecdotal recovery, successfully displacing the blocking viral fragment. Evolutionary analyses reinforce the hypothesis that cholinergic receptor interference represents a clinically significant host-pathogen interaction. Leitzke highlights a 2023 comparative genomic investigation by Romeu, which revealed that ancestral SARS-CoV-2 isolates and related bat coronaviruses from Laos and Vietnam exhibited minimal or absent furin cleavage motifs containing the proline-arginine-arginine-alanine sequence. Subsequent clinical strains isolated from human hosts, however, demonstrated complete sequence homology with human coding messenger RNA, suggesting that this receptor-blocking sequence became stabilized under selective pressure during replication within humans. Similar receptor interactions occur across unrelated pathogens: human immunodeficiency virus type 1, rabies virus, and Epstein-Barr virus have all been shown to bind acetylcholine receptors. Furthermore, in vitro research by Cheng and colleagues demonstrated that filoviruses, including Marburg virus, exploit muscarinic acetylcholine receptors for cellular entry, where competitive receptor blockade successfully prevented viral invasion. The dependence on host proteases for viral activation extends across multiple respiratory viral families, indicating that transmembrane serine protease 2 represents a broad therapeutic target. Host protease cleavage is utilized by SARS-CoV-1, Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus, seasonal coronaviruses such as HKU1, 229E, NL63, and OC43, as well as influenza A and B strains, including H1N1, H2N9, and H3N2. Cell culture studies confirm that transmembrane serine protease 2 also cleaves fusion glycoproteins of human parainfluenza viruses types 1 through 4b, human metapneumoviruses, and Sendai virus. Because viral transmissibility correlates with enzymatic affinity, deploying protease antagonists could suppress transmission across diverse pathogens. Synthetic compounds such as N-0385, nafamostat, camostat, and upamostat have demonstrated antiviral potency and human safety across randomized trials and in vitro studies, while naturally occurring compounds like bromhexine, quercetin, and epigallocatechin gallate show comparable inhibitory capabilities. Addressing acute viral transmission and downstream inflammatory surges also brings simpler biochemical interventions into focus. Antiseptic mouthwashes containing agents like hydrogen peroxide, chlorhexidine digluconate, povidone-iodine, cetylpyridinium chloride, anionic phthalocyanine derivatives, beta-cyclodextrin-citrox, or sorbitol with xylitol have demonstrated capacity to reduce oral viral load following exposure. Because mouthwashes act on the virus extracellularly before intracellular replication begins, developing viral resistance is exceptionally unlikely, avoiding the selective pressures driving vaccine-resistant mutations. In parallel, hyperactivated inflammatory cascades driven by nuclear factor kappa B can be modulated using Toll-like receptor inhibitors, including eritoran, resiquimod, resatorvid, chloroquine, and hydroxychloroquine. Leitzke contrasts these host-directed proposals with mainstream pandemic preparedness blueprints, which predominantly emphasize global genomic surveillance, expanded diagnostic testing, contact tracing, international treaty convergence, and rapid vaccine manufacturing. Although these conventional frameworks are vital, they largely overlook the conserved biological mechanisms that drive rapid infection and hyperinflammation in the human host. The review concludes that while these measures cannot guarantee complete prevention of future viral outbreaks, their widespread affordability and ease of distribution could dramatically reduce healthcare burdens and enhance global health equity, providing resilient defenses for lower-income regions with fragile healthcare infrastructure.
