records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Sunday, November 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Seven Herb Extract BNO 1030 Shows Multitarget Efficacy Against Respiratory Viruses by November 7, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Seven Herb Extract BNO 1030 Shows Multitarget Efficacy Against Respiratory Viruses Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive scientific review published in Clinical Phytoscience indicates that the standardized herbal medicine known as BNO 1030 extract exerts multivector pharmacodynamics capable of addressing acute respiratory viral infections across all phases of pathogenesis. Authored by researchers Igor Zupanets, Nataliya Bezugla, and Inna Otrishko, the paper examines how the integration of evidence-based phytotherapy into pharmaceutical care protocols offers targeted clinical benefits for widespread upper respiratory illnesses. The formulation combines seven medicinal plant extracts: marshmallow root (Althaea officinalis), chamomile flowers (Matricaria chamomilla), horsetail herb (Equisetum arvense), walnut leaves (Juglans regia), yarrow herb (Achillea millefolium), oak bark (Quercus robur), and dandelion herb (Taraxacum officinale). The authors emphasize that viral respiratory infections represent an escalating global challenge due to frequent viral mutations, rapid environmental adaptation, and modern population mobility. In response, phytoneering development combines standardized botanical cultivation with advanced processing techniques to generate a synergistic medicine delivering immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, and antibacterial activities within a single therapeutic intervention. During the initial stage of viral infection, characterized by viral attachment to respiratory mucosal membranes, cellular penetration, and subsequent intracellular replication, the extract establishes a biological barrier of phytoresistance. Chemical analyses highlighted in the review demonstrate that oak bark and walnut leaves provide rich concentrations of tannins and gallic acid that conditionally envelop viral surface structures, effectively masking them from cellular receptors and obstructing viral entry. The authors note documented antiviral efficacy against multiple common pathogens, including influenza virus type A, rhinoviruses, herpes simplex virus types I and II, and human papillomavirus. In addition, the complex blend of flavonoids derived from dandelion herb suppresses the replication of the H1N1 influenza strain and demonstrates in vitro inhibition of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. Specifically, these botanical compounds impede the critical interaction between the viral surface spike glycoprotein and the host angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 cellular receptor, thereby preventing viral entry and the propagation of newly formed viral particles. As the pathological process advances into the immune response stage, specific constituents in the botanical combination activate and modulate host defense mechanisms without inducing excessive cellular damage. Phenolic acids from horsetail herb stimulate natural killer cell counts and amplify the functional cytotoxic activity of T-killer cells, while simultaneously downregulating the synthesis of prostaglandins, cyclooxygenase-2, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha without triggering apoptosis or necrosis. Complementing this response, high-molecular-weight polysaccharides from chamomile flowers and marshmallow root heighten macrophage sensitivity and accelerate phagocytic ingestion of pathogens. Concurrently, the flavonoids apigenin and quercetin found in chamomile reduce inflammatory mediators, specifically cyclooxygenase-2, prostaglandin E2, and interleukin-6, while marshmallow polysaccharides exert an expectorant effect alongside an antitussive action stronger than that of synthetic prenoxdiazine. During the resolution phase, chamomile and dandelion flavonoids scavenge reactive oxygen species and nitric oxide, while essential oils from chamomile and yarrow exhibit broad antibacterial coverage against Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms, with yarrow-derived camphor and eucalyptol improving sputum clearance, alveolar ventilation, and pulmonary perfusion. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms Study Chemistry Order Vitamins Browse Reference The review underscores that the therapeutic reliability of the formulation stems directly from the phytoneering framework, which applies rigorous pharmaceutical controls across every phase of agricultural production and processing. By maintaining closed production cycles, cultivating designated botanical cultivars in ecologically verified regions, and applying standardized extraction methods, manufacturers achieve reproducible biochemical homogeneity and high concentrations of active phyto-constituents. According to the authors, this standardized methodology enables herbal medicines to achieve clinical efficacy comparable to conventional synthetic agents while retaining markedly superior safety parameters and multidirectional pleiotropic benefits. Safety data collected over more than twenty-five years of worldwide clinical application confirm an exceptional tolerability profile. In particular, a ten-year postmarketing surveillance study conducted in Germany identified a complete absence of serious adverse drug events, toxic overdoses, or hazardous drug-drug interactions, thereby confirming that the multicomponent phytoneering preparation can be administered safely across diverse patient demographics suffering from acute respiratory viral illnesses and related inflammatory conditions. Clinical verification of the therapeutic efficacy of BNO 1030 extract is documented through several prospective trials, including randomized controlled investigations categorized as level 1b clinical evidence. In a prospective multicenter pediatric study evaluating children between two and seventeen years of age suffering from recurrent upper respiratory tract infections, patients receiving the botanical extract demonstrated significantly faster clinical recovery times than untreated control cohorts. A six-month longitudinal follow-up verified a marked reduction in subsequent disease recurrences, with objective symptom improvement or complete clinical remission documented in more than ninety percent of treated pediatric patients. The medicine demonstrated favorable tolerance across both drops and coated tablet formulations, recording a minimal adverse event incidence of 0.47 percent consisting entirely of mild gastrointestinal disturbances. Furthermore, an assessment in children aged ten to fourteen with recurrent acute respiratory infections confirmed comprehensive clinical gains, including sleep normalization, reduced vegetative symptoms, diminished lymphadenopathy, elevated secretory immunoglobulin A levels, and normalized adaptive physiological reactions in up to ninety percent of participants. Beyond uncomplicated viral colds, the review details substantial clinical evidence supporting the medicine for treating and preventing chronic inflammatory complications within pediatric otolaryngology. In a longitudinal one-year study involving pediatric patients with chronic tonsillitis, high therapeutic success was achieved in 33.95 percent of subjects, with general treatment effectiveness recorded in an additional 46.91 percent. These clinical enhancements were confirmed through objective immunological biomarkers, including elevated serum immunoglobulin G levels and expanded absolute and relative circulating lymphocyte counts, which stabilized immune function and enabled eighty-one percent of evaluated children to avoid planned surgical tonsillectomies. Similarly, an evaluation in adolescents presenting with chronic tonsillitis complicated by concurrent perennial allergic rhinitis demonstrated rapid alleviation of inflammatory flare-ups without aggravating underlying allergic symptoms. Prolonged administration across a full year produced a greater than threefold decrease in tonsillitis exacerbation frequency, truncated symptom duration, reduced repetitive antibiotic requirements almost fourfold, and suppressed mucosal colonization by pathogenic bacteria and Candida fungi without producing drug-related adverse reactions. The botanical extract also exhibits marked regulatory actions on nasopharyngeal microbial ecology, which directly influences susceptibility to recurrent respiratory illness and secondary bacterial invasions. Prolonged infections frequently disrupt the delicate nasopharyngeal microbiocenosis and exhaust local immune barriers, including mucosal phagocytes, lysozyme production, and secretory immunoglobulin A. Clinical investigations reviewed by Zupanets and colleagues demonstrate that treatment with the extract restored healthy microbiological equilibrium in pediatric cohorts, reducing the total incidence of mucosal dysbiosis by half. Quantitative microbiological testing verified significant reductions in mucosal colonization by Staphylococcus aureus, corynebacteria, and opportunistic Candida species. Furthermore, multiple clinical studies in children with frequent recurrent viral infections corroborated substantial elevations in serum concentrations of protective immunoglobulin A, immunoglobulin M, and endogenous alpha- and gamma-interferons, establishing robust prophylactic resistance against seasonal pathogens. A distinctive pharmacological attribute detailed in the review is the extract’s capacity for selective, bidirectional regulation of innate nonspecific immune factors. In a clinical trial involving children aged two to six years diagnosed with acute respiratory viral infections, the extract demonstrated an intelligent normalizing effect on myeloperoxidase activity, an enzymatic microbicidal mediator of cytotoxic phagocytosis. When initial enzyme levels were suppressed, the formulation stimulated activity, whereas pathologically elevated baseline activity was down-regulated, preventing aggressive cytolysis and excessive tissue inflammation. This immune-modulating action curtailed nasopharyngeal microbial invasion, reducing the necessity of antibiotic prescriptions from twenty percent down to 3.3 percent, with significant symptom reduction observable by the fifth day of administration. Complementing these observations, a randomized multicenter investigation in pediatric patients presenting with nonbacterial acute tonsillitis demonstrated a four-day therapeutic gain in symptom regression, diminished reliance on nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and antipyretics, and a 59 percent reduction in overall antibiotic utilization compared with control protocols, while children with acute nasopharyngitis achieved prolonged recurrence-free remission periods. The paper also describes prominent adaptogenic and homeostatic properties of the medicine in surgical settings and explores its distinct dose-dependent immunological characteristics. Among pediatric patients undergoing surgical tonsillectomy and adenotomy procedures, preoperative treatment mitigated physiological perioperative stress, blunting abnormal cortisol surges and returning circulating cortisol to normal baseline control concentrations by the eighth postoperative day. In the postoperative phase, administration induced a nearly twofold reduction in excessive natural killer cell activity, normalized circulating interleukin-1, suppressed elevated plasma lactoferrin, and elevated protective gamma-interferon concentrations. The authors observe that the extract’s pharmacodynamics adapt to baseline host immunity and dosage levels: during acute infection, it mobilizes cytotoxic pathogen-clearance mechanisms including oxidative bursts, while during convalescence, it transitions toward anti-inflammatory cytokine modulation and antibody synthesis. Low dosing regimens primarily activate sustained immune parameters such as interleukin-6, whereas higher dosing levels mobilize acute-phase cellular defenses, including neutrophil recruitment and early interferon cascades necessary to control invasive infectious spread. In discussing the practical implementation of pharmaceutical care principles, the authors outline rational clinical recommendations for community pharmacists dispensing the formulation as an over-the-counter medicine. The extract is approved for use in both adults and pediatric patients from one year of age presenting with primary common cold symptoms such as headache, rhinorrhea, pharyngeal discomfort, generalized malaise, and arthralgia. Pharmacists can guide patients on selecting appropriate dosage forms, including oral drops, which should be shaken, held briefly within the mouth prior to swallowing, or blended into juice or tea for young children, and coated tablets swallowed whole with water. Early administration within the first forty-eight hours optimizes innate immunity, while sustained therapy across days two to five supports progressive viral clearance. By preventing common secondary complications such as acute otitis media, bronchitis, and worsening tonsillitis, the formulation curtails inappropriate antibacterial prescribing, providing demonstrable pharmacoeconomic advantages while advancing vital global healthcare initiatives aimed at curbing the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Sunday, November 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Sequential Molecular Gatekeeping Framework Explains How Animal Viruses Jump Species by November 7, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Sequential Molecular Gatekeeping Framework Explains How Animal Viruses Jump Species Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive scientific review published in Animal Diseases provides an integrative synthesis of the molecular and ecological determinants governing viral host tropism and cross-species spillover. Host tropism, which defines the specific species or cellular boundaries that a virus can successfully infect, functions as a primary evolutionary constraint on the emergence and persistence of zoonotic infectious diseases. In biological terms, this host range reflects a delicate and dynamic equilibrium between viral entry mechanisms, intracellular replication efficiency, and immune evasion strategies within the host cellular environment. When an animal virus overcomes this equilibrium and extends beyond its ancestral reservoir, spillover occurs, frequently initiating novel transmission chains with uncertain epidemiological trajectories. Focusing predominantly on high-mutation RNA viruses such as coronaviruses, orthomyxoviruses, and paramyxoviruses, the review examines how historical host coadaptation shapes susceptibility across diverse mammalian taxa, particularly in bats, rodents, and primates that harbor the vast majority of cataloged zoonotic diversity. Central to the authors’ synthesis is the formulation of the Sequential Molecular Gatekeeping Model, a conceptual architecture that organizes established virological determinants into five interdependent checkpoints spanning from receptor engagement to ecological contact. Rather than introducing uncharacterized biochemical pathways, the framework establishes a structured, stage-based hierarchy to explain how candidate pathogens navigate distinct biological hurdles. These checkpoints encompass viral receptor binding, host protease activation, intracellular immune evasion, genomic adaptability, and exposure dynamics at the ecological interface. The authors emphasize that these gatekeeping stages represent a conceptual progression rather than an obligatory linear trajectory, recognizing that their sequential order, relative importance, and mechanistic thresholds vary significantly among distinct viral families. Bidirectional interactions between checkpoints reflect the iterative nature of viral adaptation, where partial compatibility at an entry stage can exert selective pressure on downstream replication traits, ultimately determining whether an initial cross-species transmission results in an abortive spillover event or establishes self-maintaining transmission cycles. Receptor recognition constitutes the initial molecular gatekeeper of host specificity, establishing a stringent biological filter that dictates which cell types and host species can permit viral attachment. The review details how specific surface proteins and glycans govern susceptibility, such as angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronaviruses, dipeptidyl peptidase 4 for Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus, and differential sialic acid linkages for influenza A viruses. Structural studies utilizing cryo-electron microscopy demonstrate that precise electrostatic complementarity and conformational shifts, exemplified by the alternating up and down states of the coronavirus spike receptor-binding domain, dictate binding affinity. Specific amino acid substitutions, including N501Y and Q493K in coronavirus spike proteins or modifications at residues 226 and 228 in influenza hemagglutinin, alter hydrogen bonding networks and switch receptor preference between avian alpha-2,3 and human alpha-2,6 linkages. Comparative analyses demonstrate that natural receptor polymorphisms across vertebrates explain why certain mammalian taxa remain permissive while others exhibit complete docking incompatibility. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms Find Pet Care Identify Plants Read Med Journals Following receptor docking, the second molecular checkpoint requires host proteolytic activation to trigger conformational changes in viral glycoproteins necessary for membrane fusion and genome entry. For enveloped respiratory pathogens, receptor binding alone cannot execute cellular entry without cleavage by host enzymes such as transmembrane serine protease 2, furin, or endosomal cathepsins B and L. The anatomical and species-specific distribution of these proteases dictates whether viral fusion proceeds at the plasma membrane or within endosomes, directly shaping viral pathogenicity. The acquisition of a polybasic cleavage site in avian influenza hemagglutinin permits systemic cleavage by ubiquitous furin-like proteases, driving the extreme virulence observed in H5N1 and H7N9 strains. Similarly, the insertion of a multibasic furin cleavage site at the S1/S2 junction of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 enhances human transmission efficiency. Downstream of fusion, postentry replication relies on intimate host factor compatibility, illustrated by influenza polymerase subunit PB2 acquiring the E627K substitution to interact effectively with mammalian ANP32 proteins. Once inside the host cell, the invading pathogen confronts the third gatekeeping barrier: overcoming the host innate immune response governed by germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors. Cellular sensors including Toll-like receptors, RIG-I-like receptors, and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase detect viral nucleic acids, triggering cascades that synthesize type I interferons and induce hundreds of interferon-stimulated genes encoding restriction factors like tetherin, APOBEC3, and tripartite motif proteins. Zoonotic viruses counteract these host defenses through specialized viral antagonists that dampen signaling pathways. For instance, influenza A non-structural protein 1 sequesters double-stranded RNA to block retinoic acid-inducible gene I activation, while coronavirus accessory proteins execute targeted evasion, such as ORF6 inhibiting STAT1 and STAT2 nuclear translocation and ORF9b disrupting mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein complexes. Furthermore, viral papain-like proteases remove ubiquitin and ISG15 post-translational modifications from cellular substrates. Other pathogens deploy distinct evasion strategies, including rabies virus phosphoproteins inhibiting interferon cascades and flavivirus proteins directing the degradation of host STAT2 molecules. The efficacy of these immune countermeasures is intrinsically tied to host-virus coevolutionary history, as evidenced by the specialized physiological adaptations identified in natural reservoir hosts such as bats. Bats possess a constitutive low-level baseline interferon expression alongside attenuated inflammatory signaling, including dampened STING pathway activation and modified NLRP3 inflammasome responses, which allows them to harbor high viral loads without developing clinical pathology. However, when bat-borne pathogens breach species barriers into immunologically reactive hosts such as humans or swine, these same viral immune-evasion mechanisms can precipitate severe immunopathology characterized by uninhibited viral replication followed by hyperinflammatory cytokine release involving interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor alpha, and interleukin-1 beta. Beyond genetic factors, host and viral microRNAs and epigenetic chromatin remodeling contribute to this delicate immune equilibrium, shaping viral persistence and determining whether an infection remains asymptomatic or manifests as acute, fatal disease in a newly colonized recipient host. Genomic plasticity functions as the fourth gatekeeping engine, enabling RNA viruses to generate the genetic diversity required to surmount sequential host barriers. Owing to error-prone replication machinery with mutation rates ranging from 10^-3 to 10^-5 substitutions per nucleotide per replication cycle, RNA viruses exist as dynamic quasispecies that rapidly sample fitness landscapes. Beyond point mutations, major macro-evolutionary leaps occur through genomic recombination in coronaviruses, generating chimeric spike proteins with altered receptor affinities, and segment reassortment in influenza viruses, which precipitated historical pandemics including the 1957 H2N2 and 2009 H1N1 outbreaks. Successful cross-species adaptation leaves clear molecular signatures within viral genomes, such as the progressive shifting of codon usage bias to mirror host housekeeping transcripts, altered envelope glycosylation patterns that shield critical epitopes, and recurrent spike substitutions like N501Y, Q498R, and E484K. Nevertheless, stringent evolutionary constraints and transmission bottlenecks eliminate the vast majority of maladapted spillover variants that cannot balance replication fidelity with host immune escape. The fifth gatekeeping stage operates at the ecological interface, where anthropogenic and environmental factors modulate exposure rates between wildlife reservoirs, intermediate domestic hosts, and human populations. Land-use changes, extensive deforestation, agricultural intensification, and expanding human settlements disrupt natural ecosystems and erode historical geographic barriers, compelling wildlife into unprecedented contact with livestock and communities. The clearance of tropical forests in Southeast Asia, for example, has elevated exposure to bat-borne Henipaviruses including Nipah virus, while high-density animal farming creates continuous mixing vessels where cocirculating viral lineages can reassort under physiological stress. Global wildlife trade further exacerbates biosecurity vulnerabilities by transporting stressed, immunocompromised animals across biogeographic regions into crowded live-animal markets, mirroring the transmission pathways observed in severe acute respiratory syndrome outbreaks. Simultaneously, shifting thermal and precipitation patterns driven by climate change alter migratory routes and expand vector distributions, driving the geographic spread of pathogens such as West Nile virus and Rift Valley fever virus into previously non-endemic territories. To transform these retrospective molecular insights into actionable prospective biosecurity tools, the review outlines how advanced computational methodologies can operationalize the gatekeeping framework for risk-informed surveillance. High-throughput metagenomic sequencing can now detect uncharacterized viral diversity directly from field samples, while machine learning algorithms trained on receptor-binding motifs, codon usage bias, and phylogenetic data can calculate host compatibility scores. Structure-prediction platforms, molecular docking simulations, and deep mutational scanning quantitatively assess binding energetics between viral surface proteins and vertebrate receptor orthologs, accurately predicting host susceptibility as demonstrated for coronavirus affinities in felids and cervids. Integrating these in silico assessments with emerging single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics resolves cell-type-specific receptor expression and microenvironmental niches across animal tissues, while single-cell metabolomics illuminates cellular metabolic dependencies during replication. This multi-layered approach enables predictive surveillance models to evaluate which circulating animal viruses have already cleared key upstream gates, allowing public health agencies to prioritize interventions before spillover occurs. Translating the Sequential Molecular Gatekeeping Model into comprehensive global preparedness demands bridging molecular microbiology with proactive One Health governance and next-generation medical countermeasures. Conventional strain-specific vaccines frequently fail to keep pace with rapid viral evolution, emphasizing the urgent need for broad-spectrum platforms targeting structurally conserved epitopes, such as the coronavirus receptor-binding domain core or the influenza hemagglutinin stem region, presented on adaptable mRNA or nanoparticle scaffolds. Concurrently, therapeutic strategies focusing on host targets, including transmembrane serine protease inhibitors like camostat mesylate and furin antagonists, offer resilient barriers against diverse emerging lineages. However, the authors emphasize that predictive biosecurity remains constrained by severe global disparities in sequencing infrastructure, cold-chain logistics, and fragmented disease reporting, particularly across biodiverse tropical regions. Closing these operational gaps requires coordinated international investment, equitable genomic data sharing across veterinary and public health sectors, and enforceable ecosystem stewardship to mitigate viral spillover risks directly at their ecological and molecular origins. records.content: 资讯 生物在线 品牌会议 行云公开课 登录 注册 生物谷APP 搜索 最新会议 空中讲坛 热点推荐 生物在线 资讯 生物在线 品牌会议 行云公开课 活动集锦 ePoch专访 企业库 疾病库 投资库 期刊学会 热点事件 园区报道 打开APP 首页 进展 详情页 IF=81!逃逸之外还有“哑火”:四川大学魏霞蔚等团队发现一个氨基酸如何悄悄降低疫苗抗体质量 奥密克戎 F456L RBD-HR三聚体亚单位疫苗平台 来源:iNature 2026-11-03 16:37 研究者验证了“芳香族开关”的可修复性:把456位的亮氨酸换回芳香族氨基酸酪氨酸或色氨酸,抗原诱导中和抗体的能力立刻恢复。这说明这个位点不是简单“变坏就好”,而是一个可理性调节的免疫原性开关。 新冠疫情进入奥密克戎时代后,一个奇特现象引起了病毒学家的注意:F456L替换在不同奥密克戎亚系中反复独立出现。XBB.1.5在456位是苯丙氨酸(F),EG.5.1变成了亮氨酸(L),而JN.1又变回F,JN.1.16再次出现L。 这说明这个位点正承受强烈的免疫选择压力,是病毒在做适应性“微调”。但此前人们只关注F456L如何帮助病毒逃逸已有抗体,很少追问:这个突变会不会削弱疫苗诱导免疫反应的能力? 2026年10月28日,四川大学魏霞蔚等团队在Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy 在线发表题为Aromaticity at spike position 456 affects functional immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant receptor-binding domain的研究论文。 该研究把这个问题提到了关键位置。研究者采用RBD-HR三聚体亚单位疫苗平台,比较基于EG.5(含L456)和XBB.1.5(含F456)的重组疫苗免疫效果。两者序列差异极小,唯独456位点不同,结果却差异显著:虽然总抗原特异性IgG水平相当,但含L456的疫苗诱导的中和抗体滴度明显更低。也就是说,不是整体免疫应答变弱,而是“抗体数量不少,能打的不多”。 残基456处的芳香性是诱导强效中和抗体反应的关键决定因素(图源自Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy ) 为什么单个氨基酸变化会产生如此后果?研究者结合单细胞RNA测序和BCR测序发现,F456L显著削弱生发中心反应。B细胞虽然进入生发中心,但克隆扩增受限、抗体基因库重排变得贫乏,能够成熟为高亲和中和抗体的克隆被压缩。 结构建模和生物层干涉实验进一步揭示,456位残基的芳香性特别重要:芳香族侧链能与BCR形成更强的疏水和π-π相互作用,帮助BCR有效识别抗原。换成非芳香族的亮氨酸后,BCR结合亲和力下降,B细胞受体信号减弱,激活阈值提高——相当于抗原在向B细胞“低声说话”,免疫系统难以听清。 更令人振奋的是,研究者验证了“芳香族开关”的可修复性:把456位的亮氨酸换回芳香族氨基酸酪氨酸或色氨酸,抗原诱导中和抗体的能力立刻恢复。这说明这个位点不是简单“变坏就好”,而是一个可理性调节的免疫原性开关。 这项研究最重要的启示,是把“抗原逃逸”和“功能性免疫原性”明确分开。过去的疫苗更新策略主要看新变异株能否逃逸既往疫苗诱导的抗体,而现在还要追问:新的抗原序列还能不能有效激活初始B细胞、能不能支持生发中心充分成熟抗体?如果病毒通过一个氨基酸替换,在不改变总抗体量的前提下削弱中和抗体的质量,就可能出现“看似有抗体、实际防护打折”的隐蔽风险。 对下一代新冠疫苗的设计而言,这意味着不能只追求序列最新,还要评估RBD的“芳香族健康状态”。在保留关键表位的同时,确保负责BCR激活的芳香族残基位置不被病毒“偷梁换柱”。这项研究让疫苗理性设计从“追踪变异”走向“设计免疫原性”,也为理解病毒如何利用单个氨基酸重塑宿主免疫留下了一个重要范例。 参考消息:https://www.nature.com/articles/s41392-026-02939-3 版权声明 本网站所有注明“来源:生物谷”或“来源:bioon”的文字、图片和音视频资料,版权均属于生物谷网站所有。非经授权,任何媒体、网站或个人不得转载,否则将追究法律责任。取得书面授权转载时,须注明“来源:生物谷”。其它来源的文章系转载文章,本网所有转载文章系出于传递更多信息之目的,转载内容不代表本站立场。不希望被转载的媒体或个人可与我们联系,我们将立即进行删除处理。 87%用户都在用生物谷APP 随时阅读、评论、分享交流 请扫描二维码下载->
